text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Example 4.4.13.If K = G is a reductive group, and C = D-mod(FlG), then by the preceding example its character sheaf is the Grothendieck–Springer sheaf on G/G.More generally, the functor of matrix coeﬃcients for equivariant endomorphisms, cf.Equation (4.5), takes the form D-mod(B\G/B) →D-mod(G/G).This recovers the Harish-Chandra, or horocycle, transform, i.e., push-pull along the correspondence G/G ←G/B →B\G/B, where the left and middle terms are quotients with respect to the adjoint action.The latter was the point of departure for Lusztig’s study of character sheaves.Here are two related remarks.Remark 4.4.14.In the present discussion, we treated character sheaves as a direct construction, which takes as input dualizable representations and outputs adjoint equivariant D-modules.

text: GURBIR DHILLON 4.5.2.First of all, a nontrivial theorem of Beraldo [Ber17b], building on work of Gaitsgory [Gai15], states that D-mod(K) is generated by k -mod.Note that the endomorphisms of the latter are HomD-mod(K) -mod(k -mod, k -mod) ≃HomDGCatcont(k -mod, k -mod)K ≃(k -mod∨⊗k -mod)K ≃(k -mod ⊗k -mod)K ≃(k ⊕k -mod)K.Stated in words, the equivariant endomorphisms of k -mod are the category of Harish-Chandra bimodules, i.e., k-bimodules for which the diagonal action is integrated to the group K.Remark 4.5.3.We emphasize that this identity is an attractive and useful feature of the formalism.Namely, Harish-Chandra bimodules have been studied and used in representation theory for many decades and have been understood to have many favorable properties;see [BG80] and references therein.

text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 5.1.1.So far, we have discussed Beilinson–Bernstein localization and categorical representation theory for reductive groups.In the remainder of this survey, we would like to turn to their aﬃne analogues, i.e., we pass from reductive groups to loop groups.The story here is signiﬁcantly richer and is the subject of the local geometric Langlands correspondence.In this section, we will give some introductory comments on loop groups and their categorical represen- tations to prepare for a discussion of the Langlands correspondence in Section 6. 5.2.Loop groups. 5.2.1.As before, we continue to denote by G a connected reductive group over an algebraically closed ﬁeld k of characteristic zero.The main actor in this section is not G, but rather its loop group LG.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: At ﬁrst pass, just as G consists of certain matrices with entries in k, i.e., pick a faithful representation, LG consists of the same form of matrices but with entries in the ﬁeld of Laurent series k((t)).Somewhat more carefully, since we need to make sense of LG as an algebro-geometric object, it is a certain group ind-scheme whose closed points are as we just described.Example 5.2.2.Here is an explicit construction in the case when G is the (non-reductive) additive group Ga, which contains most of the representative ideas.In this case, we have Ga(k) ≃k, i.e., it is a one dimensional aﬃne space.As above, we would like LGa(k) ≃k((t)).The basic idea is that k((t)) is again an inﬁnite dimensional aﬃne space, and, in fact, by bounding the order of the pole of the Laurent series, an ascending union of pro-ﬁnite dimensional aﬃne spaces.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Explicitly as a vector space k((t)) = lim −→ n lim ←− m t−n · k[[t]]/t−n+m · k[[t]], and we use the same formula to describe its structure as an ind-scheme.That is, ﬁxing n, we obtain a pro-ﬁnite dimensional aﬃne space, which explicitly is the spectrum of a polynomial ring in countably many variables, i.e., the functions corresponding to the Taylor coeﬃcients of a series.Allowing n to vary, we obtain an ascending union of inﬁnite dimensional aﬃne spaces along closed embeddings, i.e., an ind-scheme.Remark 5.2.3.In general, LG admits a succinct description via its functor of points, which is deﬁned as follows.For any variety X, consider the functor LX from aﬃne varieties to sets whose R-points, for any k-algebra R, are LX(R) = X(R((t))).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: While this is not well-behaved for a general variety, if X is aﬃne, this is representable by an ind-scheme of ind-inﬁnite type.Taking X = G yields the loop group LG.Having given a formal deﬁnition, let us try to give a slightly more hands-on description in the spirit of Example 5.2.2.Recall the analogy between G(Fq) and G(k) and, more generally, ﬁnite G(Fq)-sets and ﬁnite dimensional G(k)-varieties as discussed in the previous sections.A basic guiding principle for the present situation is an analogy between the p-adic group G(Fq((t))) and the loop group LG.Remark 5.2.4.While some authors use the term p-adic group to mean the points of G in Qp or a ﬁnite extension thereof, here by a mild abuse of notation we call the points in any non-Archimedean local ﬁeld, such as Fq((t)), a p-adic group.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Recall that p-adic groups, with their natural topology, are ind-pro-ﬁnite sets.Explicitly, ﬁx any compact open subgroup K, i.e., a subgroup such that K ∩G(Fq[[t]]) is ﬁnite index in both K and G(Fq[[t]]).Then K is naturally an inverse limit of ﬁnite groups, and the entire group decomposes as a disjoint union of its K cosets.Concretely, for G(Fq[[t]]), the relevant inverse limit comes from the topology on power series, i.e., (5.1) G(Fq[[t]]) = lim ←− n G(Fq[t]/(tn)).

text: GURBIR DHILLON In a similar way, one can make sense of compact open subgroups of LG.Namely, one has the arc group L+G, which is a group scheme of inﬁnite type with k-points G(k[[t]]).This is deﬁned as an inverse limit of ﬁnite dimensional algebraic groups similarly to (5.1).A sub-group scheme K of LG is said to be compact open if K ∩L+G is of ﬁnite codimension in both K and L+G.Then K is naturally an inverse limit of algebraic groups, and the coset space LG/K is an ind-scheme of ind-ﬁnite type.We emphasize that, under the analogy between ﬁnite sets and ﬁnite dimensional varieties, this corresponds to being a countable discrete union of cosets in the case of p-adic groups. 5.3.D-modules on loop groups and categorical actions. 5.3.1.We would next like to discuss the convolution algebra of D-modules on LG.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Since this is an inﬁnite- dimensional object, some care is required.Its deﬁnition may be arrived at as follows.Recall that we thought of modules for D-mod(G) as akin to representations of G(Fq).In particular, the convolution algebra of D-modules itself was analogous to the group algebra Fun(G(Fq)).We would similarly like modules for D-mod(LG) to behave like representations of the p-adic group G(Fq((t))).As the latter is a topological group, one correspondingly works with smooth representations.11 For this reason, modules for G(Fq((t))) are not the same as modules for its group algebra, but instead for its Hecke algebra Dist(G(Fq((t)))) of compactly supported distributions.

text: Concretely, this can be written as the colimit (5.2) Dist(G(Fq((t)))) ≃lim −→ K Dist(K\G(Fq((t)))/K), where K runs over compact open subgroups and each Dist(K\G(Fq((t)))/K) is simply ﬁnite linear combina- tions of delta distributions on double cosets, i.e., distributions that integrate a function over a double coset KgK with respect to some Haar measure.With this in mind, the category of D-modules on the loop group is deﬁned as D-mod(LG) ≃lim −→D-mod(K\LG/K), where K runs over compact open subgroups and the colimit is taken in DGCatcont along ∗-pullback functors.It remains then to describe, for a ﬁxed K, the category D-mod(K\LG/K).However, recalling that LG/K is an ind-scheme of ind-ﬁnite type, we may moreover write it as an ascending union LG/K = [ i Xi, where each Xi is a closed subscheme of ﬁnite type that is moreover K invariant.

text: Remark 4.3.8.Remark 5.3.3.While the above construction may seem somewhat ad hoc, we should mention that it is a special case of a similar deﬁnition of D-modules for a larger class of inﬁnite dimensional varieties known as placid ind-schemes [Ras15a].In fact, a basic subtlety in this inﬁnite dimensional setting is that there are two dual versions of the category of D-modules.One comes with functoriality for ∗-pushforwards and the other with functoriality for !-pullbacks.The presentation above is for the category with ∗-pushforwards.This is the analogue of the distinction between functions and distributions on G(Fq((t))).Relatedly, the dual categories for LG may be identiﬁed after trivializing the dimension torsor, i.e., ﬁxing a compact open subgroup. 5.3.4.

text: As in the ﬁnite dimensional case, D-mod(LG) is a monoidal dg-category under convolution.In particular, as before, we can deﬁne its category of modules D-mod(LG) -mod .Here are some basic examples of representations.Example 5.3.5.If X is a placid ind-scheme acted on by LG, its category of D-modules D-mod(X) carries a canonical action of D-mod(LG) by convolution.Example 5.3.6.Given a central extension of the loop group 1 →Gm →g LG →LG →1, one obtains upon passing to Lie algebras a central extension of the loop algebra, i.e., an aﬃne Lie algebra 0 →k · 1 →bg →Lg →0.There is a canonical action of D-mod(LG) on the derived category of smooth modules bg -mod, induced by the fact that the adjoint action of g LG on bg factors through LG.

text: By deﬁnition, an object of the corresponding abelian category is a representation of bg on which 1 acts by the identity and where each vector is annihilated by a compact open subalgebra.The full dg-category, following Frenkel–Gaitsgory [FG09a], is a slight modi- ﬁcation of the naive unbounded derived category, such that objects like Verma modules or, more generally, inductions of ﬁnite dimensional representations of compact open subalgebras are compact generators.While the details of this will not be important for us, let us simply remark that the existence and utility of this modiﬁcation stem from the fact that the abelian category is of inﬁnite cohomological dimension.Relatedly, the renormalized derived category carries a t-structure and canonically identiﬁes on bounded below parts with the usual derived category.

text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.Local geometric Langlands and affine Beilinson–Bernstein localization 6.1.Overview. 6.1.1.In the previous sections, we discussed localization theory for reductive Lie algebras and explained its relation to the categorical representation theory of reductive groups.In Section 5, we met the loop groups and their categorical representations.In this ﬁnal section, we will sketch some of the basic conjectures and results in local geometric Langlands, which may be understood as parametrizing the categorical representations of loop groups.At the end, we will come full circle and meet an analogue of Beilinson–Bernstein localization for loop groups, as developed by Beilinson–Drinfeld, Frenkel–Gaitsgory, and Raskin–Yang. 6.2.A naive formulation of the correspondence. 6.2.1.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For the p-adic group G(Fq((t))), the local Langlands correspondence (conjecturally) parametrizes its irreducible representations on k vector spaces in terms of Galois theoretic data, to ﬁrst approximation homomorphisms from the absolute Galois group of Fq((t)) into the Langlands dual ˇG(k).In this subsection we would like to review what is expected and what is known about an analogous parametrization of D-mod(LG) -mod. 6.2.2.Recall that k((t)) consists of functions on a formal punctured disk D×.Following the analogy between Galois representations and local systems, cf.Appendix A, the counterparts to ˇG-valued Galois representa- tions in the present setting are ﬂat ˇG connections, i.e., ˇG de Rham local systems on D×.Concretely, these are given by connections modulo gauge equivalence, i.e., LocSys ˇ G ≃{d + ˇg((t))dt}/ ˇG(k((t))).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The same formula deﬁnes LocSys ˇ G further as an object of algebraic geometry, i.e., one takes the quotient prestack of the action of the L ˇG on the ind-scheme of connection forms d+ˇg((t))dt, which is deﬁned similarly to Example 5.2.2;see [Ras15b] for further discussion. 6.2.3.Let us try to arrive at the statement of the local geometric Langlands correspondence in a somewhat heuristic fashion.To ﬁrst approximation, we can hope that irreducible D-mod(LG) representations are in bijection with the points of LocSys ˇ G.That is, to each ˇG-connection σ one should be able to canonically attach an irreducible categorical representation Cσ of LG.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Because a general object C of D-mod(LG) -mod should decompose as a direct integral of irreducible representations, it should deﬁne a corresponding family of categories over LocSys ˇ G, whose ﬁbres over each point measure the corresponding multiplicity of Cσ in the direct integral.Since irreducibility is a feature of objects of abelian categories, this discussion is diﬃcult to formulate precisely.However, there is a good notion of a family of categories over a space, namely a quasicoherent sheaf of categories, which we review below.Modulo corrections, which we will meet duly in Equation (6.19) below, this gives the statement of the local geometric Langlands correspondence.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Namely, the conjecture is that there should be an equivalence of (∞, 2)-categories between all categorical representations of the loop group and sheaves of categories on the moduli space of local systems, i.e., (6.1) L : D-mod(LG) -mod ≃2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G).Here is a basic orienting remark.The asserted equivalence of 2-categories is not saying that for a given categorical representation C, the underlying dg-categories of C and L(C) are equivalent.Rather, it is saying that, for any pair of objects C and D, there is an equivalence HomD-mod(LG) -mod(C, D) ≃Hom2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G)(L(C), L(D)), and these are compatible with composition as one varies C and D.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Remark 6.2.4.As a toy model, a Morita equivalence for usual algebras A -mod ≃B -mod matches not the underlying vector spaces of modules, but only their homomorphisms.Explicitly, one can consider, for a ﬁnite dimensional k vector space V , the Morita equivalence V ⊗−: Vect ≃End(V ) -mod .This exchanges k and V , which certainly are not isomorphic, but on endomorphisms we do have HomVect(k, k) ≃k ≃HomEnd(V )(V, V ).Before turning to corrections, we would like to ﬁrst discuss sheaves of categories and some of the basic compatibilites L is expected to satisfy. 6.2.5.To discuss sheaves of categories, let us start with the case of an aﬃne variety X = Spec OX.In this case, a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories on X is simply an OX-linear, as opposed to merely k-linear, dg-category.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Since OX-linearity is the same as being able to tensor by complexes of OX-modules, we have equivalently that 2-QCoh(X) ≃QCoh(X) -mod .In particular 2-QCoh(pt) is simply DGCatcont, and, for any closed point pt →X, one has a pullback Vect ⊗ QCoh(X)−: 2-QCoh(X) →DGCatcont, i.e., one can speak of the ﬁbres of a sheaf of categories, which are usual dg-categories.In this way, one thinks of a sheaf of categories as a family of categories over X.Remark 6.2.6.More generally, given any map f : X →Y pullback deﬁnes a monoidal functor QCoh(Y ) → QCoh(X), and, in particular, adjoint induction and restriction functors f ∗: 2-QCoh(Y ) ⇆2-QCoh(X) : f∗.Here is a basic example of a sheaf of categories.Example 6.2.7.Given a map ˜X →X of varieties, QCoh( ˜X) is a QCoh(X)-algebra and, in particular, a sheaf of categories over X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For any point x of X, the ﬁbre of the sheaf of categories is, by Example 4.2.25, simply the quasicoherent sheaves on the actual ﬁbre, i.e., i∗ x QCoh( ˜X) ≃QCoh( ˜X × X x). 6.2.8.For a general X, not necessarily aﬃne, the deﬁnition proceeds by gluing, exactly as in the deﬁnition of quasicoherent sheaves.While the details are not so important for us, we should mention the following beautiful phenomenon established by Gaitsgory in [Gai15].Namely, for general X, one by deﬁnition produces sheaves of categories by patching them aﬃne by aﬃne.On the other hand, one also has the global monoidal category of quasicoherent sheaves and hence its category of left modules QCoh(X) -mod.One can therefore ask for the relation between the two.As for usual quasicoherent sheaves, one has a global sections functor (6.2) Γ : 2-QCoh(X) →QCoh(X) -mod .

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For usual sheaves, the analogous map Γ : QCoh(X) →Γ(X, OX) -mod is rarely an equivalence if X is not aﬃne.13 By contrast, for most ﬁnite dimensional X, e.g., any algebraic stack of ﬁnite type, the functor (6.2) is an equivalence, a phenomenon called 1-aﬃneness.A basic conjecture in the subject, due to Gaitsgory, is that LocSys ˇ G is also 1-aﬃne;see [Ras15b].This is a subtle assertion, as 1-aﬃneness does not hold in general for ind-schemes or classifying stacks of group 13For the reader wondering about the use of ‘rarely’, the point is that when one considers the full derived algebra of global functions, Γ can still be an isomorphism for non-aﬃne varieties, e.g., for open subvarieties of aﬃne varieties.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON Categorical representations of LG Sheaves of categories on LocSys ˇ G D-mod(GrG) QCoh(pt / ˇG) D-mod(Flaﬀ G ) QCoh(eN/ ˇG) D-mod(LG/LN, ψ) QCoh(LocSys ˇ G) bgκc -mod QCoh(Op ˇ G) Figure 1.Some objects (conjecturally) exchanged under local geometric Langlands. schemes of inﬁnite type.So, in some sense, one needs the two types of issues to ‘cancel out’ for LocSys ˇ G.This was partially addressed in an important work of Raskin [Ras15b], which showed that (6.2) is fully faithful for X = LocSys ˇ G . 6.3.Properties of the correspondence I. 6.3.1.Having dispensed with a discussion of deﬁnitions, let us get to the heart of the matter and discuss what L is expected to look like.More precisely, let us list a few basic objects on each side that are expected to be exchanged with one another.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Combined with a compatibility with parabolic induction, this is expected to largely pin down the equivalence.The structure of our discussion will be as follows.We have listed the categories exchanged in Figure 1.For each row in the ﬁgure, we will spend a little time describing the objects that appear on either side and motivate why one should expect them to be exchanged.Finally, we will see what matching intertwining operators amounts to in these cases and, in particular, we will meet the promised correction of (6.1). 6.3.2.For the ﬁrst two examples from Figure 1, it is clarifying to recall some basic features of p-adic representation theory.By smoothness, any representation π of a p-adic group contains nontrivial invariants πK for all suﬃciently small compact open subgroups K.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For such a K, if π is irreducible, the ﬁxed vectors πK will be an irreducible representation of the Hecke algebra Dist(K\G(Fq((t)))/K), which naturally acts on it by convolution.In this way, one obtains a bijection between irreducible representations of G(Fq((t))) containing K-invariant vectors and irreducible representations of this Hecke algebra.As one shrinks the subgroup K, the corresponding Hecke algebra grows, and this gives a basic measure of the complexity of a representation.Namely, for a given irreducible π, one can ask for a maximal K for which one has nontrivial invariants, and, in some sense, the larger K is, the less complicated π is.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the other side of local Langlands, the (Weil–Deligne variant of the) absolute Galois group of Fq((t)) carries a canonical ﬁltration by descending normal subgroups called the ramiﬁcation ﬁltration.For a given ˇG(k)-valued Galois representation, one can measure its complexity by asking through what quotient of this ﬁltration the action factors.A basic and striking organizing principle is that these two measures of complexity are exchanged under local Langlands.14 14More precisely, the depth of a representation, which is a certain nonnegative rational number deﬁned by Moy–Prasad [MP94], should coincide with the slope of the corresponding Galois representation, as measured by the upper numbering ramiﬁcation ﬁltration.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.4.Properties of the correspondence II: unramiﬁed representations. 6.4.1.From the preceding discussion, it follows that the most easily understood representations of p- adic groups should be those that have ﬁxed vectors with respect to the maximal compact open subgroup G(Fq[[t]]).15 Similarly, the simplest Galois representations should be those on which the action factors through the ﬁnal quotient of the ramiﬁcation ﬁltration, i.e., they extend to ˇG-local systems on the non- punctured disk.Explicitly, these are precisely the representations which factor through the Galois group of the residue ﬁeld (6.3) 1 →I →Gal(Fq((t))s/Fq((t))) →Gal(Fq/Fq) ≃bZ →1, where the superscript ‘s’ denotes the separable closure.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Since one actually works with the Weil group, which by deﬁnition replaces bZ with Z, unramiﬁed Galois representations, up to isomorphism, are speciﬁed by elements of ˇG, up to conjugacy.That is, we follow the image of 1 ∈Z under a map Z →ˇG.In this simplest case, local Langlands reduces to the Satake isomorphism between the spherical Hecke algebra and the character ring of ˇG, i.e., Dist(G(Fq[[t]])\G(Fq((t)))/G(Fq[[t]])) ≃Fun( ˇG(k)/ ˇG(k)), where the right hand side denotes the adjoint invariant polynomial functions on ˇG, viewed as a variety over Spec k [Sat63].By passing to their characters, we obtain that irreducible unramiﬁed representations of G(Fq((t))) are parametrized by (semisimple) conjugacy classes in ˇG(k), as desired.Remark 6.4.2.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For the reader encountering these ideas for the ﬁrst time, we emphasize that even the com- mutativity of the appearing Hecke algebra is not a priori obvious.This is illustrative of how passing to bi-invariant distributions for a large compact subgroup dramatically simpliﬁes life. 6.4.3.To prepare for the geometric version, we should mention that each irreducible unramiﬁed represen- tation embeds, uniquely up to scaling, into the universal unramiﬁed representation (6.4) Fun(G(Fq((t)))/G(Fq[[t]])).Moreover, to extract each from the universal case, one takes the submodule of (6.4) which transforms by the corresponding character under right convolution by the spherical Hecke algebra.Finally, let us discuss the analogues of the above in local geometric Langlands.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the automorphic side, we consider the category of D-modules on the aﬃne Grassmannian D-mod(GrG) = D-mod(LG/L+G) as a substitute in a way that is hopefully familiar by now to the above universal unramiﬁed representation.On the spectral side, any de Rham local system on the punctured disk that extends to the full disk is trivializable, i.e., we obtain the stacky point pt / ˇG →LocSys ˇ G and correspondingly view QCoh(pt / ˇG) as a sheaf of categories over LocSys ˇ G.We should also mention that one has analogues of not only the universal case, but also of an individual irreducible unramiﬁed representation.We defer a more detailed discussion until Section 6.9.Remark 6.4.4.We should note that, while the unramiﬁed case is the most basic, it is completely fundamental in both arithmetic and geometric Langlands.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Namely, in the global Langlands correspondence, which we do not discuss in detail here, any irreducible smooth representation of the adelic group G(AF ) factorizes as a restricted tensor product of irreducible representations of the p-adic groups G(Fx) at each place, and all but ﬁnitely many are unramiﬁed.To even make sense of such an inﬁnite tensor product, one makes essential use of the fact that unramiﬁed representations have canonical generating lines, namely their spherical invariants.In the global geometric theory, almost all that is known so far is for the analogue of everywhere unramiﬁed (or possibly tamely ramiﬁed) automorphic representations. 15We should note that, for groups other than GLn, there are other non-conjugate maximal compact subgroups.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.5.Properties of the correspondence III: unramiﬁed principal series. 6.5.1.Given the unramiﬁed representations of p-adic groups, one can produce further representations as follows.As in other parts of representation theory, one has parabolic induction functors that allow one to build representations of G starting with representations of smaller groups, such as the Cartan T .Feeding unramiﬁed representations into this construction yields an important family of modules, the unramiﬁed principal series.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Their simple subquotients are precisely the simple G(Fq((t)))-modules with nontrivial in- variants for the compact open Iwahori subgroup I, i.e., the preimage of the Borel of B(Fq) of G(Fq) under the projection G(Fq[[t]]) →G(Fq).16 That is, applying parabolic induction to unramiﬁed representations yields the next simplest family of repre- sentations of p-adic groups.In spectral terms, such irreducible representations of G(Fq((t))) correspond to Galois representations that are tamely ramiﬁed with unipotent monodromy.To explain this, recall from the sequence (6.3) the inertia subgroup I ≃Gal(Fq((t))s/Fq((t))), where Fq denotes an algebraic closure of Fq.The next quotient in the ramiﬁcation ﬁltration splits this as 1 →Iwild →I →Itame →1.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The basic idea for Itame, the tame inertia, is that it behaves like its characteristic zero counterpart, i.e., covers of a formal punctured disk over k.These covers are classiﬁed exactly like the covering spaces of a circle in topology, i.e., one adjoins an nth root of t for a positive integer n.In positive characteristic, these are separable if and only if n is coprime to the characteristic of q, and such covers exhaust all Galois extensions of degree coprime to q.Explicitly, one may choose an isomorphism Itame ≃Π ℓZℓ, where ℓruns over primes not equal to the characteristic of Fq.A Galois representation is said to be tamely ramiﬁed if it factors through the quotient by Iwild, and it is further said to be unipotently monodromic if any element of Itame, or equivalently a topological generator, is sent to a unipotent element of ˇG. 6.5.2.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: To orient ourselves for the geometric discussion, let us review in slightly more detail how the relevant parabolic induction of p-adic representations goes.Given the Borel B, whose Levi quotient is the abstract Cartan T , one obtains a correspondence on rational points T (Fq((t))) ←B(Fq((t))) →G(Fq((t))), where the leftward arrow is a surjection with kernel the rational points of the unipotent radical N(Fq((t))), and the rightward arrow is a closed embedding.This gives rise to a functor of parabolic induction, (6.5) T (Fq((t))) -mod Res −−→B(Fq((t))) -mod Ind −−→G(Fq((t))) -mod .Explicitly, one inﬂates a smooth representation π of T (Fq((t))) to a representation of B(Fq((t))) by having the unipotent radical act trivially, and then one induces up to G(Fq((t))).

text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Remark 6.5.3.For a reader who has not explicitly encountered parabolic induction before, it may be orienting to realize that the classiﬁcation of irreducible algebraic representations of reductive groups by their highest weight is an example of parabolic induction.Indeed, for the algebraic groups G, B, T and N as above, one has adjunctions between their categories of algebraic representations over any ﬁeld Rep(G) Res ⇄ Ind Rep(B) CoinvN ⇄ Res Rep(T ), where Res denotes restriction, CoinvN denotes the functor of N coinvariants, and Ind is the functor of coinduction.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Concatenating these, one obtains the functor of parabolic restriction, which takes a G-module and returns its N-coinvariants, viewed as a T -module, as well as its right adjoint functor of parabolic coinduction, which takes a T -module, extends it to a B-module with a trivial action of N, and coinduces this to G.With this, the theorem of the highest weight, which can be phrased as each irreducible G-module having a line of N-coinvariants, in particular implies that every irreducible G-module appears as a submodule of a parabolically coinduced module.Moreover, in characteristic zero, by complete reducibility it follows that every irreducible coincides with a parabolically coinduced module.

text: Via the explicit model of the coinduction of a character as sections of a line bundle, this recovers the Borel–Weil theorem about sections of line bundles on G/B. 6.5.4.Let us turn to the geometric case.In this case, the automorphic side will similarly be D-modules on a semi-inﬁnite ﬂag manifold, i.e., D-mod(LG/L+T · LN), which, as before, may be constructed from D-mod(GrT ) by a suitable functor of parabolic induction similar to (6.5).Remark 6.5.5.Here is a technical comment regarding this category.It is as yet unknown how to treat the space LG/L+T · LN as an object of algebraic geometry.However, its category of D-modules may be deﬁned by enforcing smooth descent, i.e., by taking the D-mod(L+T ·LN) invariants of D-mod(LG).

text: GURBIR DHILLON From this discussion, it follows that the pullback is given by (6.7) QCoh(LocSys ˇ B) ⊗ QCoh(LocSys ˇ T ) QCoh(pt / ˇT) ≃QCoh(LocSysP × LocSys ˇ T pt / ˇT) ≃QCoh(ˇn/ ˇB).Finally, the pushforward again yields QCoh(ˇn/ ˇB) viewed as a sheaf of categories on LocSys ˇ G via the projection (6.8) ˇn/ ˇB →LocSys ˇ B →LocSys ˇ G .It is clarifying to slightly rewrite this purely in terms of ˇG.To do so, we may tautologically rewrite our stack in terms of the cotangent bundle of the ﬂag variety, i.e., ˇn/ ˇB ≃( ˇG ˇ B× ˇn)/ ˇG =: eN/ ˇG.Explicitly, eN is the moduli space of pairs ( ˇB′, X), where ˇB′ is a Borel subgroup and X is an element of its unipotent radical.With this, the projection (6.8) may be written via the Springer resolution, i.e., as a composition eN/ ˇG →ˇg/ ˇG →LocSys ˇ G .

text: Here, the ﬁrst map sends a pair ( ˇB′, X) to X, and the second map is deﬁned similarly to (6.6) (but is very far from an isomorphism).Remark 6.5.7.As we will review in Section 6.8.25 below, the relationship between principal series represen- tations of G and coherent sheaves on the Springer resolution for ˇG showed up ﬁrst in the p-adic theory. 6.5.8.The two preceding examples, namely the ﬁrst two rows of Figure 1, concern objects of low ramiﬁca- tion.These cases of the local geometric Langlands correspondence, while the most basic, are already serious results.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Indeed, on the one hand, as we mentioned before, they are suﬃcient local inputs for the simplest cases of the (conjectural) global geometric Langlands correspondence, where one studies D-modules on the moduli space of G-bundles on a global curve, possibly with parabolic reductions at ﬁnitely many points.On the other hand, they have important applications within usual representation theory.A notable example is their implications for the representation theory of critical level aﬃne Lie algebras, which we will discuss in more detail in Section 6.9 below.Another key application, after passing to sheaves with modular coeﬃcients,18 is to the modular representation theory of reductive groups;see [FM99], [MV07], [AR15], [RW18], [BGM+19], [BRR20], [BRar] and references therein, as well as the surveys [Wil17], [CW21].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Given the importance of these developments, it is rather remarkable that they only skim the surface of the full conjecture, i.e., equate only very small subcategories of each side.Indeed, in spectral terms, the previous cases concern the full subcategory of 2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G) supported on the formal neighborhood of local systems with regular singularities and unipotent monodromy, which is the smallest in an inﬁnite increasing sequence of loci whose union exhausts LocSys ˇ G.The next two examples of the correspondence which we discuss, by contrast, concern categorical loop group representations and sheaves of categories on LocSys ˇ G with arbitrary ramiﬁcation.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.6.1.In many situations in representation theory, e.g., algebraic representations of reductive groups or (g, B)-modules, irreducible representations admit a canonical generating line, namely the highest weight vectors.By contrast, for the p-adic group G(Fq((t))), most irreducible modules do not admit a canonical generating line, roughly due to the noncommutativity of Dist(K\G/K) for all suﬃciently small K.Remark 6.6.2.For unramiﬁed representations, there is a canonical generating line, namely the G(Fq((t)))- invariants.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This basic miracle, i.e., the commutativity of the spherical Hecke algebra, is crucial in the subject, e.g., for the tensor product factorization of adelic representations and the reduction of the study of unramiﬁed automorphic representations to the study of Hecke eigenfunctions and eigensheaves.However, if one asks instead for a canonical line not inside π, but rather as a quotient of π, the situation is better.Namely, there is a canonical functor from G(Fq((t))) -mod to vector spaces, which sends each irreducible to either a line or zero.This is the functor of Whittaker coinvariants and may be understood as follows.To approximate the deﬁnition, we may ﬁrst consider a seemingly direct analogue of highest weight theory, namely the Jacquet functor of N(Fq((t)))-coinvariants Jac : G(Fq((t))) -mod →Vect, π 7→πN(Fq((t))).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: While this is very useful, it sends many interesting irreducible representations to zero19 and others to greater than one dimensional vector spaces.To correct for this, one twists the construction by a generic character of N(Fq((t))).Explicitly, let us index the simple roots by i ∈I, and consider the composition (6.9) ψ : N(Fq((t))) →(N/[N, N])(Fq((t))) ≃Π i Fq((t)) sum −−→Fq((t)) res −−→Fq, where sum is the addition of Laurent series and res sends a Laurent series to its residue, i.e., the coeﬃcient of t−1.By composing this with a suitably generic character Fq →k×, one obtains a character of N(Fq((t))), which we again denote by ψ, and the Whittaker coinvariants are given by Whit : G(Fq((t))) -mod →Vect, π 7→πN(Fq((t))),ψ.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This sends simple modules to either a line or zero, with the crucial property that many cuspidal representa- tions, e.g., all for G = GLn, are sent to lines.A basic property here is that Whit admits a right adjoint, given by sending k to the space of Whittaker functions Fun(G(Fq((t)))/N(Fq((t))), ψ), i.e., the coinduction of ψ to G(Fq((t))). 6.6.3.The above constructions admit the following geometric analog.First of all, the homomorphism of topological groups (6.9) lifts to a map of group ind-schemes ψ : LN →L(N/[N, N]) ≃Π i LGa →LGa →Ga.From here, we would like to pull back from Ga the analogue of a generic character.Recalling the analogy between the trivial representation of G(Fq) and the tautological categorical action of G on Vect, we therefore need a generic action of Ga on Vect.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: An action of an algebraic group H on Vect is the same data as a character sheaf on H, i.e., a D-module χ equipped with a suitably associative isomorphism µ!χ ≃χ ⊠χ, where µ : H×H →H denotes the multiplication map.We emphasize that in contrast to the broader usage of character sheaf in Section 4.4, which was the analogue of the character of a ﬁnite dimensional representation of 19This phenomenon is more or less the existence of cuspidal representations, i.e., of simple G(Fq((t)))-modules that may not be found inside parabolically induced modules.We emphasize that this is a basic fact of life in the p-adic setting and in the simpler setting of ﬁnite groups of Lie type, which is absent in the algebraic representation theory of reductive groups.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON G(Fq), the present usage of character sheaf is the analogue of a character, i.e. one dimensional representation, of G(Fq).Remark 6.6.4.Slightly more informally, if for any closed point h of H we write χh for the corresponding !-stalk of χ, the above is giving isomorphisms of stalks χh1h2 ≃χh1 ⊗χh2, for h1, h2 ∈H.That is, a character sheaf gives a homomorphism into lines, i.e., the invertible elements of Vect♥, just as a character gives a homomorphism into nonzero scalars, i.e., the invertible elements of k.With this, the analogue of a generic character of Fq is the exponential D-module exp(z) on Ga.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Explicitly, if we write z for the standard coordinate on Ga ≃A1, this D-module stores the diﬀerential equation satisﬁed by the exponential function ez, i.e., exp(z) ≃DGa/(DGa · (∂z −1)), and its multiplicativity essentially follows from the identity ez1+z2 = ez1 · ez2.With this, we write ψ for the corresponding character sheaf on LN, i.e., ψ!exp(z), and we may again form the functor of Whittaker coinvariants Whit : D-mod(LG) -mod →Vect, C 7→CLN,ψ and the category of Whittaker D-modules (6.10) D-mod(LG/LN, ψ).Before turning to its spectral counterpart, we would like to make a few orienting comments.Remark 6.6.5.Let us try to provide three ways of thinking about the analogy between the exponential D-module on Ga(k) and a generic character of Gq(Fq).The ﬁrst way is rather down to earth.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For simplicity, let us suppose that Fq coincides with its prime subﬁeld Fp.In this case, if we write e2πi/p for a nontrivial pth root of unity in k×, a concrete choice of generic character is Fp →k×, a 7→ea·2πi/p, and any other diﬀers by multiplication by a nonzero element of Fp.That is, a generic character looks like an exponential.The same holds, mutatis mutandis, for a nontrivial extension Fq, where one ﬁrst uses the trace map Fq →Fp.The second way is also rather practical.Namely, for a k vector space V , its character sheaves are in canonical bijection with closed points of V ∗, where to a covector ξ one attaches the character sheaf ξ!exp(z).In particular, for V = Ga, there is only one nontrivial choice of character sheaf up to dilation by Gm, just as there is only one nontrivial character for Fq up to dilation by F× q .

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The third way is more general and goes via the functions-sheaves correspondence.To begin, a beautiful feature of positive characteristic is an interesting self-isogeny of any commutative group scheme H over Fq, the Lang isogeny, which takes the form 1 →H(Fq) →H →H →1, i.e., it cuts out as its kernel the ﬁnite group of rational points.For H = Ga, this is concretely the short exact sequence 1 →Ga(Fq) →Ga x7→xq−x −−−−−−→Ga →1.Pushing forward the constant sheaf along this isogeny and taking its direct summands yields a family of character sheaves on Ga indexed by irreducible representations of Ga(Fq).Upon taking trace of Frobenius, these character sheaves yield exactly the irreducible characters of Ga(Fq).That is, characters of Fq have canonical lifts to character sheaves on Ga.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS correspondence with exp(z) in characteristic zero then ﬁts into a broader analogy between wildly ramiﬁed Galois representations and de Rham local systems with irregular singularities.Remark 6.6.6.Let us comment on the deﬁnition of the category of Whittaker D-modules D-mod(LG/LN, ψ).This is deﬁned by taking the (LN, ψ)-coinvariants of D-mod(LG), similarly to the categories of D-modules on semi-inﬁnite ﬂag manifolds.It is also identiﬁed with the (LN, ψ)-invariants by an important theorem of Raskin [Ras21].While an identiﬁcation of Whittaker invariants and coinvariants does not literally hold in the p-adic setting, it is analogous to the compact approximation of the Whittaker model by Rodier [Rod75]. 6.6.7.Let us now describe the expected spectral counterpart to the Whittaker model.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This is simply QCoh(LocSys ˇ G), i.e., all quasicoherent sheaves on the moduli of local systems.The basic intuition here again can be taken from the p-adic setting.Namely, each irreducible represen- tation π of G(Fq((t))) has, at most, a line of Whittaker coinvariants.It will be convenient to work instead with Hom(indG(Fq((t))) N(Fq((t))) k−ψ, π) =: ℓ, where ind is the functor of compactly supported induction.This identiﬁes with the Whittaker coinvariants of the contragredient representation of π and, in particular, is again a line or zero.On the other hand, under local Langlands one associates to π a Galois representation σ and imagines π as ‘sitting over’ σ in the space Gal ˇ G of Galois representations.In the modern formulations of arithmetic local Langlands as an equivalence of categories, cf.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Section 6.10 below, it is expected that any π admitting nonzero Whittaker coinvariants is exchanged with a one dimensional skyscraper sheaf L(π) supported over σ.Moreover, this line canonically associated to π is expected to simply be ℓ.So, combining the identiﬁcations Hom(indG(Fq((t))) N(Fq((t))) kψ, π) ≃ℓ≃Hom(OGal ˇ G, Lπ), we see that L ought to exchange the (compactly) induced Whittaker module and the structure sheaf OGal ˇ G.In the geometric setting, we have already replaced the Whittaker module by the corresponding space of D-modules D-mod(LG/LN, ψ).20 Similarly, we replace the structure sheaf OGal ˇ G by QCoh(LocSys ˇ G), which again corepresents global sections, but now of sheaves of categories.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: As we will shortly discuss when we get to intertwining operators, this correspondence leads to many striking and concrete conjectures in geometry and representation theory.However, for now let us conclude our discussion of this row of Figure 1 with a couple remarks.Remark 6.6.8.Unlike in the p-adic setting, where not every tempered irreducible representation admits a Whittaker model, the expectation in local geometric Langlands is that every tempered D-mod(LG) repre- sentation does.The basic idea is the following.For a point x of a stack X with isotropy group Ix, the abelian category of quasicoherent sheaves on X scheme theoretically supported at x identiﬁes with Rep(Ix), and in particular the skyscraper will not generate unless Ix is unipotent.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Under local arithmetic Langlands, this matches Shahidi’s generic packet conjecture, which states that, within a tempered L-packet,21 exactly one irreducible representation will admit a Whittaker model [Sha90].By contrast, the skyscraper module Vect for QCoh(X) will generate the subcategory of 2-QCoh(X) supported at x, and in this sense every irreducible tempered module is generic.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Despite this, it will not be the case that D-mod(LG/LN, ψ) is a generator for D-mod(LG), for issues having to do with the promised correction to the naive formulation (6.1). 20Note that the diﬀerence between induction and compact induction disappears, due to Raskin’s identiﬁcation of Whittaker invariants and coinvariants [Ras21]. 21Beyond the case of GLn, the map from irreducible representations of G(Fq((t))) to Galois representations is not a bijection, but instead ﬁnite-to-one, and the ﬁbres are called L-packets.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.7.Properties of the correspondence V: Kac–Moody representations. 6.7.1.We have arrived at the last row of Figure 1, and here something rather remarkable occurs.Namely, we will meet a conjectural property of the correspondence, proposed by Frenkel–Gaitsgory [FG06a], which concerns Kac–Moody representations.As such, it has no p-adic counterpart and is an aspect of local Langlands which is special to the geometric context.Remark 6.7.2.We should mention that the importance of Kac–Moody representations in geometric Lang- lands ﬁrst appeared in the global story.Namely, as we alluded to Section 3.4.13, a method of construction for automorphic D-modules, due to Beilinson–Drinfeld, is via localization of Kac–Moody representations.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This may be understood as a global analogue of the work of Frenkel–Gaitsgory and was the ﬁrst instance where the relationship to conformal ﬁeld theory provided tools unavailable in the arithmetic setting. 6.7.3.We would ﬁrst like to give the reader a basic feel for Kac–Moody algebras.Their study for a general connected reductive group essentially reduces to the case when g is simple.So, to avoid mostly notational distractions, we shall assume that G is a simply connected, almost simple group.First, we begin with the loop algebra g((t)) ≃g ⊗ k k((t)).This is simply the extension of scalars of g to the ﬁeld of Laurent series.Explicitly, the bracket takes the form [X ⊗f, Y ⊗g] = [X, Y ] ⊗fg, X, Y ∈g, f, g ∈k((t)).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: It is clarifying to think of it as the space of maps from the punctured disk D× to g, where the Lie bracket is performed pointwise.That is, it is the inﬁnitesimal symmetries of the trivial G-bundle on the punctured disk.Let us regard the loop algebra as an inﬁnite dimensional Lie algebra over k.A basic fact of life is that many k vector spaces that naively seem like g((t))-modules in fact carry an action of a central extension, i.e., of an aﬃne Lie algebra 0 →k · 1 →bg →g((t)) →0.Remark 6.7.4.This may be understood as an instance of the general phenomenon that quantization of ﬁeld theories introduces anomalies for their local symmetries.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Fortunately, all the possible central extensions of the loop algebra admit a simple classiﬁcation – they are in canonical bijection with the line of invariant bilinear forms on the ﬁnite dimensional algebra g.Explicitly, to such a form κ ∈(g∗⊗g∗)G, one associates the central extension 0 →k · 1 →bgκ →g((t)) →0, where the bracket of 1 with anything is zero, by centrality, and the other brackets are modiﬁed by [X ⊗f, Y ⊗g] = [X, Y ] ⊗fg −κ(X, Y ) Res(f · dg). 6.7.5.For a level κ, let us denote the category of smooth bgκ-modules on which the central element 1 acts via the identity by bgκ -mod, cf.Example 5.3.6.If κ is integral, meaning the extension of the loop algebra arises from a central extension of LG, then, as discussed in Example 5.3.6, this category carries an action of D-mod(LG), and we therefore shall focus on this case.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Recalling that G was assumed to be simple and simply connected, the integral levels form a lattice Z֒ →(g∗⊗g∗)G, generated by the so-called basic form, which explicitly gives the short coroots squared length two.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.7.6.A basic observation in the study of representations of aﬃne Lie algebras is that as one varies the level κ, the corresponding representation theory has two ‘phases.’ Namely, for all suﬃciently negative deﬁnite κ, the representation theory behaves similarly.For example, all Verma modules have ﬁnite length, and the character formulas for their simple quotients across these levels take essentially the same form [KT95].Likewise, for all positive deﬁnite κ, the representation theory behaves similarly as one varies the level.Here, the Verma modules now have inﬁnite length, and the character formulas for their simple quotients do not substantially vary with the level [Kas90].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: We may therefore anticipate that there is a special level κc, the critical level, where the representation theory undergoes a phase transition.Naively, one might expect this central point to be the zero form.Instead, due to an aﬃne analogue of the ρ-shift in the representation theory of g, it is minus half of the Killing form, i.e., κc = −1 2 · κKilling. 6.7.7.As one might expect, the behavior of the representation theory at the phase transition, i.e., at critical level, displays many features not present at other levels.A fundamental such property was discovered by Feigin and Frenkel [FF91].Namely, while the center of the enveloping algebra22 at noncritical levels is trivial, i.e., only scalars, they showed that the center at critical level was nontrivial.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Crucially, they further identiﬁed it with the algebra of functions on the moduli space Op ˇ G of ˇG-opers on the punctured disk.While we will momentarily recall its precise deﬁnition, at ﬁrst pass the main point is that representation theory at the critical level has local Langlands duality, particularly the geometry of ˇG-connections, hardwired into it. 6.7.8.To ﬁrst approximation, a ˇG-oper consists of a ˇG bundle with a connection and a ˇB reduction, which are suitably transverse.Let us spell this out explicitly.Recall that to speak of Langlands dual groups, one ﬁxes pinnings of G and ˇG and, in particular, Chevalley generators fi, ˇαi, ei, i ∈I, of ˇg.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: If we write f for the element of ˇg such that (f, 2ˇρ, Σ i ei) form an sl2 triple, then the space of ˇG-opers is the moduli space of connections (6.11) Op ˇ G ≃{d + fdt + ˇb((t))dt}/L ˇN.By thinking of the trivial bundle as equipped with its tautological ˇB-reduction, the term fdt in the above formula implements the aforementioned transversality of the connection and the reduction.For alterna- tive formulations of the deﬁnition of an oper, e.g., with the advantage of visibly being independent of the coordinate t, see for example [BD04].The formula (6.11) may be read as taking a certain aﬃne subspace of all connections d + ˇg((t))dt on the trivial ˇG bundle and quotienting by the adjoint action of L ˇN.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Indeed, (6.11) is the Hamiltonian reduction of the aﬃne space d + ˇg((t))dt with respect to a generic character of L ˇN and, in particular, carries a canonical Poisson structure.Gelfand–Dikii and Drinfeld–Sokolov [DS84] studied its Poisson geometry in the context of integrable hierarchies prior to its appearance in geometric Langlands;for g = sl2 this recovers the celebrated KdV hierarchy.Here are two orienting remarks for a reader who has not encountered this moduli space before.Remark 6.7.9.Although Op ˇ G is presented as space of connections modulo the action of a loop group, similarly to LocSys ˇ G, its geometry is astronomically simpler.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: In fact, it is simply an inﬁnite dimensional aﬃne space, and, in particular, its points do not have automorphisms. 22As a technical remark, we mean the center of the appropriate completed enveloping algebra, or equivalently the Bernstein center of the abelian category of smooth bgκ-modules.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON Remark 6.7.10.The previous remark is typically proven by showing every L ˇN orbit is simply transitive, i.e., without nontrivial stabilizers, and exhibiting an explicit slice intersecting each orbit exactly once.It can be clarifying to note that this whole story, including the above argument, is an aﬃne analogue of a work of Kostant [Kos63].Namely, he showed that one has a canonical isomorphism ˇg// ˇG ≃(f + ˇb)/ ˇN, i.e., that a similar ﬁnite dimensional Hamiltonian reduction of ˇg cuts out a copy of the Poisson center.Moreover, he showed the natural quantizations of both sides are matched, namely that the center Z(ˇg) may be cut out from U(ˇg) via a quantum Hamiltonian reduction with respect to ˇN. 6.7.11.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Via the projection map Op ˇ G →LocSys ˇ G, where one passes from an oper to its underlying connec- tion, we may view QCoh(Op ˇ G) as a sheaf of categories over LocSys ˇ G.With this, it is expected that bgκc -mod is exchanged with QCoh(Op ˇ G) under local geometric Langlands, so that the tautological monoidal functor QCoh(Op ˇ G) →Hom2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G)(QCoh(Op ˇ G), QCoh(Op ˇ G)) is exchanged, via the Feigin–Frenkel isomorphism OOp ˇ G ≃Z(bgκc), with the central action Z(bgκ) -mod →HomD-mod(LG) -mod(bgκc -mod,bgκc -mod).In the next subsections, we will discuss several interesting conjectures this correspondence yields about representation theory at critical level.However, we would like to already mention here one particularly striking consequence.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: It is known that any ˇG-connection σ admits an oper structure χ, i.e., the projection Op ˇ G →LocSys ˇ G is surjective on k- points [FZ10].By the above, it formally follows that the ‘irreducible’ categorical representation Cσ of the loop group, which corresponds to the skyscraper Vect over σ, is given by (6.12) bg -mod ⊗ QCoh(Op ˇ G) Vect, i.e., the category of Kac–Moody representations with central character χ.On the one hand, this gives a uniform conjectural construction of all the Cσ via Kac–Moody represen- tations, i.e., the spectral to automorphic direction of the local geometric Langlands correspondence.On the other hand, this predicts that for any two opers χ, χ′ lying over σ, the corresponding categories of Kac–Moody modules are equivalent, which is by itself a deep conjecture in representation theory.Remark 6.7.12.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: In fact, due to the correction to the naive formulation (6.1) of local geometric Langlands, which we have yet to explain, the category (6.12) is really a full subcategory of Cσ.In practice, this means that one obtains Cσ by renormalizing (6.12), cf.Section 6.9 for further discussion. 6.7.13.This completes our introductory discussion of the objects appearing in Figure 1.However, before going further, we should emphasize that there are many more expected compatibilities coming from the arithmetic story and connections with physics, cf.Section 6.10 below.We cannot help but mention one particularly spectacular example of this.Braverman–Finkelberg have proposed for G = GLn a candidate for the Langlands dual to the convolution algebra D-mod(LGLn) itself [BF19].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This is based on physical considerations, ultimately going back to a striking formula for computing S-dual boundary conditions for four dimensional N = 4 Yang–Mills theory discovered by Gaiotto-Witten [GW09].Explicitly, they conjecture that D-mod(LGLn) is exchanged under local Langlands duality with coherent sheaves on the moduli space parametrizing degenerate ﬂags of local systems, i.e., local systems Li of rank i, 1 ⩽i ⩽n, along with not necessarily injective maps of connections Li →Li+1, 1 ⩽i < n.An arithmetic analogue of this conjecture has since been formulated by Zhu [Zhu21].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.8.Intertwining operators.Next, we would like to explain how considering the intertwining operators between the categories appearing in Figure 1 recovers several fundamental theorems and produces many striking conjectures.At this point, the promised technical correction to the naive formulation (6.1) of the local geometric Langlands correspondence naturally asserts itself in the following manner. 6.8.1.Recall the simplest representations in the p-adic setting are the unramiﬁed ones.Pleasantly, we will already meet the necessary correction to the naive formulation (6.1) of the geometric conjecture in the unramiﬁed case.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: To see this, recall that local Langlands ought to exchange the D-modules on the aﬃne Grassmannian D-mod(GrG) with quasicoherent sheaves on the trivial bundle QCoh(pt / ˇG).In particular, their endomor- phisms ought to be canonically identiﬁed, so let us see what they are.On the automorphic side, recalling that GrG is the coset space LG/L+G, as in Section 4 we have (6.13) HomD-mod(LG) -mod(D-mod(GrG), D-mod(GrG)) ≃D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G), also known as the derived Satake category of bispherical sheaves.As a potential warning for readers encoun- tering this for the ﬁrst time, this category is not the derived category of the corresponding abelian category, but instead richer.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the spectral side, using that the map ˇg/ ˇG →LocSys ˇ G is formally ´etale at the trivial bundle, we may compute, as in Example 4.2.25, that (6.14) Hom2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G)(QCoh(pt / ˇG), QCoh(pt / ˇG)) ≃QCoh(pt / ˇG × LocSys ˇ G pt / ˇG) ≃QCoh(pt × ˇg pt / ˇG).A couple points of explanation are in order.First, for the last equivalence in (6.14), one may use the following general observation.Suppose one has varieties X, Y, and Z acted upon by an algebraic group K.Then, given a K equivariant correspondence X →Z ←Y, one has a canonical isomorphism of quotient (derived) stacks X/H × Z/H Y/H ≃(X × Z Y )/H.We will use this fact repeatedly going forwards without further comment.Second, we also remind the reader that the appearing ﬁbre products in (6.14) are derived schemes.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Concretely, this just means we also remember the Tor, so that the self-intersection pt × ˇg pt is the spectrum of the exterior algebra Sym ˇg∗[1], by a standard calculation using Koszul resolutions.We can therefore naively hope for an equivalence of monoidal categories between (6.13) and (6.14).Instead, the derived Satake equivalence, which is an important theorem of Bezrukavnikov–Finkelberg [BF08], identiﬁes (6.13) with an enlargement of (6.14).More precisely, they proved an equivalence (6.15) D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G) ≃IndCohnilp(pt / ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G pt / ˇG), where the right hand side is the monoidal category of ind-coherent sheaves with nilpotent singular support. 6.8.2.Let us brieﬂy indicate what is meant by an ind-coherent sheaf, and what it means to impose a singular support condition.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: These are admittedly somewhat technical corrections to the idea of a quasicoherent sheaf, and may be safely skipped by a reader meeting this circle of ideas for the ﬁrst time.We begin with ind- coherent sheaves, and then turn to the singular support condition.In the simplest possible terms, the theory of ind-coherent sheaves stems from the diﬀerence between ﬁnitely generated modules and ﬁnitely generated projective modules, i.e., vector bundles.In the abelian category,

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON say for an aﬃne scheme X, there are certainly fewer vector bundles than ﬁnitely generated modules, unless X is a disjoint union of reduced points.However, in the derived category, the distinction is subtler.Indeed, if X is smooth, then any ﬁnitely generated module admits a ﬁnite resolution by vector bundles.For this reason, one cannot distinguish between ﬁnite complexes of ﬁnitely generated modules and ﬁnite complexes of vector bundles.If X is not smooth, they again diﬀer in the derived category, as a general ﬁnitely generated module now needs an inﬁnite projective resolution.Explicitly, one could take the skyscraper sheaf at any singular point of X.In particular, the distinction between these types of complexes gives a measure of the singularities of X. 6.8.3.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Let us treat the preceding paragraphs more carefully, following Krause [Kra05] and Gaitsgory [Gai13].To begin with, recall that, for an algebraic variety X, its category of quasicoherent sheaves QCoh(X) is compactly generated by the perfect complexes, i.e., objects locally equivalent to ﬁnite complexes of vector bundles.If X is aﬃne, this reduces to the tautology that OX -mod is generated by the ring of regular functions OX.For non-aﬃne X, the claimed generation is straightforward for quasi-projective varieties, but is in general a somewhat delicate theorem of Thomason [TT90].As the global analogue of ﬁnite complexes of ﬁnitely generated modules, consider the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves Coh(X)b ⊂QCoh(X).By deﬁnition, IndCoh(X) is its ind-completion, i.e., IndCoh(X) is compactly generated by Coh(X)b.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Plainly, objects of IndCoh(X) are formal colimits of bounded complexes with coherent cohomology, and complexes of homomorphisms are computed as the homotopy limit of complexes HomIndCoh(X)(lim −→ i Ei, lim −→ j Fj) ≃lim ←− i lim −→ j HomQCoh(X)(Ei, Fj).For any coherent sheaf E, this formula forces HomIndCoh(X)(E, −) to commute with colimits, which fails in QCoh(X) unless E is perfect.Since perfect complexes are bounded coherent, one obtains upon ind-completing their inclusion functor an adjunction QCoh(X) ⇄IndCoh(X), where the left adjoint is fully faithful and an equivalence if X is smooth.In particular, one thinks of IndCoh(X) as an enlargement of QCoh(X), and one has a truncation of any ind-coherent sheaf to a quasi- coherent sheaf.Morever, IndCoh(X) carries a natural t-structure and agrees with QCoh(X) on bounded below objects.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Informally, one obtains IndCoh(X) by adjoining objects concentrated in cohomological degree −∞.Remark 6.8.4.It may be orienting to recall that we already met such renormalizations of derived categories of inﬁnite cohomological dimension when discussing Kac–Moody representations and D-modules on the loop group, cf.Example 5.3.6.Remark 6.8.5.The idea of systematically distinguishing between perfect and bounded coherent complexes on singular varieties also arose earlier in algebraic geometry, e.g., the quotient IndCoh(X)/ QCoh(X) is the ind-completion of Orlov’s singularity category [Orl04]. 6.8.6.Let us next explain the idea of singular support, as developed by Gulliksen [Gul74], Eisenbud [Eis80], Avramov, and Buchweitz [AB00] for complete intersections, and extended by Arinkin–Gaitsgory to derived complete intersections [AG15a];

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: see also the important [BIK08].By deﬁnition, the diﬀerence between ind- coherent and quasicoherent sheaves stems from singularities of X, and, in particular, the quotient IndCoh(X)/ QCoh(X) will be supported along the singular locus of X.Given a coherent sheaf F, one might like an invariant of it that records, to ﬁrst approximation, where along the singularities of X it fails to be perfect.Singular support provides a reﬁned answer to this question.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Here is a slightly more precise formulation.Let us suppose X is a quasi-smooth derived scheme, i.e., one whose cotangent complex T ∗(X) is supported in cohomological degrees -1 and 0.Then, given an object F as above, its singular support is a closed conical subset Λ of H−1T ∗(X).The singular support measures, aﬃne by aﬃne, the local nilpotence of elements of OX, recovering the usual support, as well as certain natural degree two self-maps of F.Moreover, given any such subset Λ, one obtains the full subcategory IndCohΛ(X) ⊂IndCoh(X) of ind-coherent sheaves with singular support contained in Λ.For example, if Λ is the zero section, this recovers QCoh(X).Although we will not provide a general deﬁnition of how to compute singular support, we will discuss some special cases momentarily.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: First, however, we include a few orienting remarks.Remark 6.8.7.A derived scheme is quasi-smooth if and only if it locally may be written as a ﬁbre product X ×Z Y , where X, Y , and Z are smooth varieties.In this local picture, the cotangent complex takes the following explicit form.Namely, for a point (x, y) of the ﬁbre product with common image z, one has a distinguished triangle of tangent complexes (6.16) T(x,y)(X ×Z Y ) →Tx(X) ⊕Ty(Y ) →Tz(Z) +1 −−→.For the reader unfamiliar with this distinguished triangle, it may be helpful to ﬁrst understand the case when X and Y map transversally to Z.Here, the ﬁbre product is again smooth, and the above distinguished triangle becomes a hopefully intuitive short exact sequence.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For the general case, the point is that the derived structure on the ﬁbre product modiﬁes its tangent complex so that the most naive modiﬁcation of the transverse situation holds.Upon dualizing (6.16), one sees that H−1 of the cotangent bundle is concretely the codirections ξ ∈T ∗ z (Z) normal to the images of Tx(X) and Ty(Y ) or, even more informally, the remaining directions to walk in Z.An important special case of the preceding is a ﬁbre product of the form (6.17) {0} ×An Y, i.e., the derived vanishing locus of n functions f1, . . . , fn on Y .In this way, quasi-smoothness is an example of the hidden smoothness philosophy in derived algebraic geometry.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Namely, while the underlying classical scheme of the ﬁbre product may be arbitrarily singular, it underlies a derived scheme that behaves like a complete intersection, i.e., is only mildly singular.Let us next explain what singular support amounts to in a few examples.Example 6.8.8.For a coherent sheaf F, the intersection of its singular support with the zero section is simply the usual support.Example 6.8.9.Suppose X may be exhibited as a hypersurface in a smooth variety U.In this case, H−1T ∗(X) consists of X, thought of as the zero section, along with a line ℓx placed at each singular point x of X.Suppose a coherent sheaf F contains such an x in its usual support.Then its singular support contains ℓx if and only if F is not isomorphic to a perfect complex in any Zariski neighborhood of x.Example 6.8.10.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Suppose X is given, as in the spectral side of derived Satake, as the self-intersection of the origin in a vector space X = 0 × V 0.In this case, one has that T ∗ (0,0)X ≃V ∗[1].Here, singular supports may be understood as usual supports on the other side of Koszul duality.Namely, the skyscraper sheaf k generates IndCoh(X), which yields upon taking its endomorphisms an equivalence IndCoh(X) ≃Sym V [−2] -mod .

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON Via this identity, for any coherent sheaf F, its singular support agrees with the usual support of the corre- sponding Sym V [−2]-module, ignoring grading shifts.One can replace 0 and V here by any smooth point of any variety. 6.8.11.Having discussed the basics of ind-coherent sheaves and singular support, let us return to the derived Satake equivalence, i.e., (6.18) D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G) ≃IndCohnilp(pt / ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G pt / ˇG).In this equivalence, the subscript ‘nilp’ refers to the subcategory of ind-coherent sheaves with singular support lying in the nilpotent cone N ⊂ˇg∗≃H−1T ∗(pt / ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G pt / ˇG). 6.8.12.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: As we will see shortly, the pattern encountered in the unramiﬁed case, where one has to enlarge the spectral side by allowing ind-coherent sheaves with nilpotent singular support, occurs in several other cases of matching intertwining operators.This necessitates tweaking the spectral side of local geometric Langlands, which is accomplished by passing from quasicoherent sheaves of categories to ind-coherent sheaves of categories with nilpotent singular support 2-QCoh(LocSys ˇ G) ⇝2-IndCohnilp(LocSys ˇ G).We will touch on what this means momentarily, but for now let us say that with this correction, we obtain the current formulation of the local geometric Langlands conjecture, namely an equivalence (6.19) D-mod(LG) -mod ≃2-IndCohnilp(LocSys ˇ G). 6.8.13.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Let us brieﬂy sketch the theory of ind-coherent sheaves of categories with singular support, which is due to Arinkin [Ari18].When one increases the categorical level from ind-coherent sheaves to ind-coherent sheaves of categories, to set up a theory of singular support one no longer asks that the base variety X be quasi-smooth, i.e., has its cotangent complex in degrees -1 and 0, but instead that it be smooth, i.e., has its cotangent complex in degree 0.We will see why momentarily.So, let X be a smooth algebraic variety.Using 1-aﬃneness, one can show that, for any proper map f : Z →X from a smooth variety, QCoh(Z) compactly generates the full subcategory of 2-QCoh(X) consisting of objects supported over im(f).In particular, this subcategory identiﬁes with modules for the convolution algebra QCoh(Z × X Z).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The (∞, 2)-category of ind-coherent sheaves of categories on X has the following basic properties.First, it carries a monoidal action of 2-QCoh(X), so that one can speak of the supports of objects.Moreover, it is generated by objects of the form QCoh(Z), for Z as above.However, the endomorphisms of such an object are now increased to IndCoh(Z × X Z), which, roughly speaking, grows larger relative to its quasicoherent analog as Z →X becomes further from a smooth map.More precisely, as in Remark 6.8.7, the singular support of objects in this convolution category lie along codirections in X normal to the tangent bundle of Z × Z.As a consequence, the less smooth f is over a given point x, the more ind-coherent sheaves of categories supported over x lie in the subcategory of 2-IndCoh(X) generated by QCoh(Z).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: In particular, QCoh(Z) will no longer generate a full subcategory of 2-IndCoh(X) corresponding to objects supported over im(f), but rather the following microlocal reﬁnement.23 Since we assumed f is proper, we 23Explicitly, to see that a reﬁnement is necessary, note that, in its absence, by taking Z = X we would equate 2-IndCoh(X) and 2-QCoh(X).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS may form the conormal variety N ∨ Z, i.e., the closed isotropic subvariety of T ∗X obtained by projecting the kernel of f ∗T ∗X →T ∗Z along Z × X T ∗X →T ∗X.One can associate to any ind-coherent sheaf of categories its support in T ∗X, and QCoh(Z) generates the full subcategory of objects with microsupport lying in N ∨ Z.More generally, given any closed, conical isotropic subvariety Λ of T ∗X, one associates the full subcategory 2-IndCohΛ(X) ⊂2-IndCoh(X).This is again generated by the (truncations) of QCoh(Z), with endomorphisms IndCohΛ(Z × X Z), where now Λ is used to impose a usual singular support restriction on usual ind-coherent sheaves as in Remark 6.8.7.In particular, taking Λ to be the zero section, we recover 2-QCoh(X).Remark 6.8.14.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: An alternative approach to the formalism of ind-coherent sheaves and ind-coherent sheaves of categories, including a theory of singular supports beyond the quasi-smooth and smooth cases, respectively, is under development by di Fiore–Stefanich. 6.8.15.The previous discussion does not literally apply to LocSys ˇ G.This is because, due roughly to its inﬁnite dimensionality, it is not a smooth Artin stack.However, it is expected that it carries a similar theory of ind-coherent sheaves of categories.Admitting the existence of such a formalism, it only remains from (6.19) to explain what the singular support condition ‘nilp’ refers to.However, this should not be surprising given what we met in the unramiﬁed case.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Namely, the cotangent complex to LocSys ˇ G at a connection (ˇP, ∇) is given by the de Rham complex computing the ﬂat sections on the punctured disk of the coadjoint bundle (6.20) ˇP ˇ G× ˇg∗.In particular, the cotangent space, i.e., its zeroth cohomology, canonically identiﬁes with the ﬂat sections of (6.20).With this, ‘nilp’ cuts out within each cotangent space the ﬂat sections which are nilpotent. 6.8.16.Having dealt with the necessary corrections, let us at last have the promised fun and inspect the categories of intertwining operators between the objects in Figure 1.In this way, we will meet many beautiful theorems and conjectures, which will hopefully give the reader more of a hands-on feel for this subject.On either side, all the appearing categories are self-dual.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For the categories of D-modules and quasico- herent sheaves, up to manageable issues of an inﬁnite dimensional nature, this follows from Example 4.4.6.We will discuss the case of Kac–Moody representations in more detail in Section 6.8.35 below.Admitting this self-duality, via the canonical equivalences HomD-mod(LG) -mod(C, D) ≃HomD-mod(LG) -mod(D∨, C∨), and similarly for categories over LocSys ˇ G, we need only write down the categories of intertwining operators ‘above the diagonal.’ We record these intertwining operators in Figures 2 and 3.The calculations of these categories on the automorphic and spectral sides essentially follow the pattern of those performed in Section 4, particularly Example 4.2.25 and the discussion of Section 4.3.9.

text: The ﬁrst equivalence (6.21) D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G) ≃IndCohnilp(pt / ˇG × pt / ˇG) is one we have already met, namely the derived Satake equivalence of Bezrukavnikov–Finkelberg [BF08].The derived Satake equivalence is t-exact and on abelian categories recovers the geometric Satake equiv- alence D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G)♥≃QCoh(pt / ˇG) = Rep( ˇG), which is an earlier fundamental theorem due to Lusztig [Lus83], Drinfeld, Ginzburg [Gin95], Mirkovi´c– Vilonen [MV07].Both equivalences, but slightly more transparently the abelian one, categorify the analogous assertion in the p-adic setting Dist(G(Fq[[t]])\G(Fq((t)))/G(Fq[[t]])) ≃K0(Rep( ˇG)) ⊗ Z k, which, along with its mixed characteristic counterpart, is an isomorphism due to Satake [Sat63].Let us make two comments about this.Remark 6.8.18.
