text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS The basic point here is that there are only countably many L+G × L+G orbits on LG, and these are naturally indexed by irreducible representations of ˇG.More carefully, any cocharacter ˇµ : Gm →T yields, upon restriction to the formal disk about the origin, a point of LT , which we denote by tˇµ.If we let ˇΛ+ denote the dominant cocharacters, LG is then stratiﬁed by the orbits L+G · tˇµ · L+G, for ˇµ ∈ˇΛ+.But these are the highest weights of ˇG-modules, and the equivalence exchanges the corresponding intersection cohomology complexes on GrG and simple ˇG-modules.Remark 6.8.19.Second, here is an orienting comment.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The underlying space on the automorphic side of derived Satake parametrizes triples (P1, P2, τ), where P1 and P2 are G-bundles on the disk and τ is an identiﬁcation of them on the punctured disk.Similarly, the underlying space on the spectral side parametrizes triples (E1, E2, τ), where E1 and E2 are ˇG-connections on the formal disk and τ is an isomorphism of their restrictions to the punctured disk.Note that since every ˇG-connection on the formal disk is trivializable, the underlying classical stack is pt / ˇG.However, this moduli problem is asking us to intersect pt / ˇG with itself in LocSys ˇ G, which aﬀords the derived structure crucial to making the equivalence hold.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Thus, somewhat informally speaking, the equivalence exchanges constructible objects on a coherent moduli space for G with coherent objects on an analogous constructible moduli space for ˇG. 6.8.20.The next equivalence of the table, namely D-mod(L+G\LG/I) ≃IndCohnilp(pt / ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G eN/ ˇG) is also a very nice theorem due to Arkhipov–Bezrukavnikov–Ginzburg [ABG04].As in Remark 6.8.18, we may count parameters as follows.On the automorphic side, the relevant stratiﬁcation of LG is now by the strata L+G · tˇµ · I, for ˇµ ∈ˇΛ.That is, to shrink from having L+G to I on the right, we must grow by a factor of the ﬁnite Weyl group, i.e., from dominant cocharacters to all cocharacters.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the spectral side, recalling that eN is the cotangent bundle to the (ﬁnite) ﬂag variety, we are considering ˇG-equivariant coherent sheaves on a derived thickening of the zero section, i.e., of the ﬂag variety itself.Here, up to ignoring the thickening, the same lattice ˇΛ occurs in QCoh(Fl ˇ G / ˇG) ≃QCoh( ˇB\ ˇG/ ˇG) ≃QCoh( ˇB\ pt) ≃Rep( ˇB), as equivariant line bundles on Fl ˇ G or, equivalently, the characters of Rep( ˇB). 6.8.21.We next pair the spherical and Whittaker categories to obtain D-mod(L+G\LG/LN, ψ) ≃QCoh(pt / ˇG).This is also a known and important theorem due to Frenkel–Gaitsgory–Vilonen [FGV01].It may be under- stood as a geometric reﬁnement of the Casselman–Shalika formula from p-adic representation theory [CS80], which explicitly determines the Whittaker covector of an unramiﬁed representation.

text: GURBIR DHILLON Remark 6.8.22.Let us also brieﬂy comment on a basic diﬀerence with the bi-spherical situation, i.e., derived Satake.There, the spectral side is a derived enhancement of Rep( ˇG).Roughly speaking, this occurs since the stalks of the intersection cohomology sheaves on L+G\LG/L+G are quite interesting along orbit closures and correspond to q-weight multiplicities for ˇG-representations [Lus83].In the present case, one has no such derived enhancement.This occurs because the intersection cohomology objects on L+G\LG/LN, ψ are clean, i.e., have vanishing !-stalks and ∗-stalks along the boundary of the open orbit in their support. 6.8.23.

text: Finally, let us pair spherical vectors and Kac–Moody representations to obtain bgκc -modL+G ≃QCoh(Opunramiﬁed ), where by deﬁnition the latter moduli space parametrizes oper structures on the trivial bundle, i.e.Opunramiﬁed ≃pt / ˇG × LocSys ˇ Op ˇ G.This is also a known theorem, due to Frenkel–Gaitsgory [FG09b], which contains and strengthens many prior results about L+G-equivariant Kac–Moody representations at critical level due to Feigin–Frenkel, Beilinson–Drinfeld, and others.In this case, the Grothendieck groups are no longer countable.Instead, one has continuous families of simple modules parametrized by pro-ﬁnite dimensional aﬃne spaces.Nonetheless, we can give the following rough count.

text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.8.25.We are ready to move on to the next row of Figures 2 and 3, i.e., the case of tame ramiﬁcation and unipotent monodromy.We ﬁrst meet the endomorphisms, i.e., a monoidal equivalence (6.22) D-mod(I\LG/I) ≃IndCohnilp(eN/ ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G eN/ ˇG).This attractive statement is remarkable for many reasons.For one, there is not such a coherent realization of the ﬁnite Hecke category, and, in this sense, the equivalence really is something particular to the aﬃne setting and, speciﬁcally, its connection with arithmetic.25 As with other statements of low ramiﬁcation we have met so far, it is a celebrated theorem due to Bezrukavnikov [Bez16].As far as we know, this equivalence was ﬁrst formulated as a conjecture by Ginzburg [CG10].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: A major motivation comes from the p-adic setting, where an analogous isomorphism between Dist(I\G(Fq((t)))/I), i.e., the aﬃne Hecke algebra, and an appropriate specialization of the equivariant K-theory of the Steinberg variety eN × ˇg eN is due to Kazhdan–Lusztig [KL87].They, and independently Ginzburg, used this isomorphism to classify the irreducible representations of aﬃne Hecke algebra and determine their characters.Equivalently, they determined the characters of the simple subquotients of the unramiﬁed principal series of G(Fq((t))).Let us count parameters.On the automorphic side, the relevant stratiﬁcation of LG has constituents I · w · tˇµ · I, for w ∈Wf and ˇµ ∈ˇΛ.

text: This is an aﬃne analogue of the Bruhat decomposition of G into the double cosets B ·w ·B, for w ∈Wf, and indeed the indexing set here is the (extended) aﬃne Weyl group Wf ⋉ˇΛ.Note that, as in Section 6.8.20, we once again shrink from L+G to I, and therefore our stratiﬁcation grows by a factor of Wf.On the spectral side, these parameters arise as follows.To begin, note that the Steinberg variety26 explicitly parametrizes triples (X, ˇB′, ˇB′′), where X is a nilpotent element of ˇg and ˇB′, ˇB′′ are two Borel subgroups containing it.The Steinberg is the union of Wf many locally closed Lagrangians in eN × eN, where each Lagrangian is speciﬁed by the relative position of ˇB1 and ˇB2, i.e., a point of ˇB\ ˇG/ ˇB.Remark 6.8.26.Recall that we are really interested in the quotient eN/ ˇG × ˇg/ ˇ G eN/ ˇG.

text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.8.27.Let us now pair the unramiﬁed principal series and Whittaker model to obtain an equivalence (6.24) D-mod(I\LG/LN, ψ) ≃QCoh(eN/ ˇG).This assertion is again known, and is a very nice theorem of Arkhipov–Bezukravnikov [AB09].Their argu- ment is widely regarded as one of the gems in this subject.The result plays a basic role in Bezrukavnikov’s proof of (6.22), in parallel to the role of an analogous identity in K-theory for the identiﬁcation of the aﬃne Hecke algebra with the equivariant K-theory of Steinberg by Kazhdan–Lusztig.The parameter count here goes as follows.On the automorphic side, it is slightly more convenient to pass to the semi-inﬁnite variant, i.e., (6.25) D-mod(LN · L+T \LG/LN, ψ).

[CD21].Remark 6.8.29.We rewrote the automorphic side of (6.24) in semi-inﬁnite terms in (6.25).This was to minorly simplify the combinatorics of relevant orbits.However, there are less frivolous reasons to bear this alternative expression in mind.Namely, recall that parabolic induction for categorical representations really does produce the semi-inﬁnite version of the aﬃne ﬂag variety, cf.Section 6.5.Relatedly, in the proof of Arkhipov–Bezukravnikov, it is objects of semi-inﬁnite origin, e.g., the Wakimoto sheaves, which play a central role. 6.8.30.By pairing the unramiﬁed principal series with Kac–Moody representations, we arrive at an equiv- alence bgκc -modI ≃QCoh(eN/ ˇG × LocSys ˇ G Op ˇ G).

text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS 6.8.31.Let us pass to the third row of Figures 2 and 3 and study intertwiners out of the Whittaker model.We ﬁrst meet its endomorphisms and an equivalence of monoidal categories (6.27) D-mod(LN, ψ\LG/LN, ψ) ≃QCoh(LocSys ˇ G).This is a striking and essentially wide open conjecture.Even symmetric monoidality for the left hand side is far from obvious.Morally, it is a manifestation of the uniqueness of Whittaker covectors in the current geometric setting under the usual correspondence between multiplicity freeness and commutative endomorphism algebras.We emphasize that this equivalence would pin down an enormous swathe of Conjecture (6.19), namely all the sheaves of categories on the spectral side with singular support along the zero section.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Such categorical representations are called tempered.Remark 6.8.32.Although (6.27) is very much open, here is a special case which is known.Namely, by work of Raskin [Ras21], the depth ﬁltration on categorical representations of the loop group gives rise to a ﬁltration on D-mod(LN, ψ\LG/LN, ψ), with each quotient a monoidal colocalization.The ﬁrst quotient, corresponding to representations with vectors ﬁxed by the prounipotent radical of an Iwahori subgroup, is the Iwahori–Whittaker category D-mod(˚I, ψ\LG/˚I, ψ).This in turn admits a further quotient, which corresponds to passing from all tamely ramiﬁed representations to those with unipotent monodromy, namely the Steinberg–Whittaker category D-mod(˚I, ψ, s \LG/˚I, ψ, s).

[CD21].If we write N∧for the formal completion of ˇg along the nilpotent cone N, we have a monoidal equivalence D-mod(˚I, ψ, s \LG/˚I, ψ, s) ≃QCoh(N∧/ ˇG), which is the promised piece of (6.27).Bezrukavnikov proved the equivalence of aﬃne Hecke categories (6.22) essentially by combining this with the previously mentioned result of Arkhipov–Bezrukavnikov.More precisely, let us write eN∧for the formal completion of the Grothendieck–Springer variety eˇG := ˇG ˇ B× ˇb along the Springer variety.

text: GURBIR DHILLON Namely, the aﬃne Skryabin theorem of Raskin30 gives, for any level κ, a canonical equivalence bgκ -modLN,ψ ≃Wκ -mod, where Wκ is the aﬃne W-algebra.On the other hand, at the critical level Feigin–Frenkel had identiﬁed Wκc with the center Z(bgκc) of the enveloping algebra [FF91], and therefore also with OOp ˇ G.This in combination with the aﬃne Skyrabin theorem yields (6.28).Remark 6.8.34.The reader may wish to consult the survey of Arakawa in the present volume for more details about the W-algebra;see also [Ara17], [FBZ04].Here let us only mention in passing that the aﬃne Skryabin theorem enables the systematic use of techniques from categorical representation theory in the study of representations of W-algebras.

text: As an example, one can see [DR20], which discusses localization theory for highest weight modules for W-algebras. 6.8.35.In the ﬁnal row, we meet the endomorphisms of Kac–Moody representations.These are identiﬁed with aﬃne Harish-Chandra bimodules at critical level as follows.First, the category bgκc -mod is canonically self-dual as a D-mod(LG) representation and, in particular, as an abstract dg-category.To see this, it is orienting to begin with a simpler case.For a ﬁnite dimensional Lie algebra a with a central extension 0 →k · 1 →eac →a →0, consider the category eac -mod of eac-modules on which 1 acts via the identity.

text: If we write ea−c for the opposite central extension, e.g., given by the additive inverse of any representing 2-cocycle, one has a perfect pairing eac -mod ⊗ea−c -mod →a -mod →Vect, where the ﬁrst arrow tensors together representations to cancel the extensions, and the second is Lie algebra homology.In the aﬃne case, it was shown by Arkhipov–Gaitsgory [AG15b], building on previous work of Frenkel– Gaitsgory [FG06b], that for any κ the composition bgκ -mod ⊗bg−κ+2κc -mod →bg2κc -mod →Vect is a perfect pairing, where the ﬁrst arrow tensors representations, and the second arrow is the functor of semi- inﬁnite cohomology.Brieﬂy, this is the natural homology theory for representations of inﬁnite dimensional Lie algebras like bg (formally, Tate Lie algebras), but it requires a central extension of level 2κc.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: One has such a duality statement for general Tate Lie algebras, cf. [Ras20b], [Dhi21].In particular, one has a self-duality bgκc -mod ⊗bgκc -mod →Vect, which is another sense in which the critical level is the midpoint of the space of levels.Moreover, as in Section 4.5.2, this identiﬁes the D-mod(LG) equivariant endofunctors of bgκc -mod with the category of critical level aﬃne Harish-Chandra bimodules bgκc ⊕bgκc -modLG .This is a beautiful, if somewhat elusive, category.For example, all of its objects lie in cohomological degree −∞with respect to the natural t-structure on bgκc ⊕bgκc -mod, i.e., it consists of homological phantoms introduced through renormalization.Remark 6.8.36.The aﬃne Harish-Chandra bimodules at other levels are also subtle, with some of the basic works and conjectures due to I.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Frenkel–Malikov [FM97] and Gaitsgory [Gai07]. 30We note in passing that Skryabin is an anagram of ‘by Raskin.’

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS For these bimodules, local geometric Langlands predicts a monoidal equivalence with the spectral convo- lution algebra bgκc ⊕bgκc -modLG ≃QCoh(Op ˇ G × LocSys ˇ G Op ˇ G).This is a striking and essentially wide open conjecture.To our knowledge, even the spherical case and the case of tame ramiﬁcation with unipotent monodromy are open, though we expect they are within reach using some of the aforementioned work of Frenkel–Gaitsgory, cf.Sections 6.8.23 and 6.8.30, combined with the localization theorem at critical level, which we now turn to. 6.9.Localization theory. 6.9.1.We would like to discuss an important application of ideas and techniques from local geometric Langlands to a problem purely within the representation theory of aﬃne Lie algebras.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: We begin by setting up the context. 6.9.2.Recall that in Section 3 we discussed localization theory for reductive Lie algebras and sketched how it was used to determine the characters of the simple highest weight modules.For aﬃne Lie algebras, an analogous program was developed at noncritical levels by Kashiwara–Tanisaki in a series of works [Kas90], [KT90], [KT95], [KT96], [KT98], [KT00].Brieﬂy, at negative level they identiﬁed D-modules on the aﬃne ﬂag manifold with certain Kac–Moody representations.At positive level, they did the same, but instead with D-modules on the thick aﬃne ﬂag manifold, a scheme of inﬁnite type parametrizing G-bundles on P1 with full level structure at zero and a Borel reduction at inﬁnity.As a consequence, they obtained the characters for simple highest weight modules at noncritical levels.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: After their work, it was understood that to make inroads on the remaining case, namely the representation theory at critical level, one would need further ideas and tools.We would like to now sketch what localization theory looks like here, following work of Beilinson–Drinfeld, Frenkel–Gaitsgory, and Raskin–Yang. 6.9.3.The basic new complication at critical level is that the geometric side of the localization theorem is not simply D-modules on a space, but a tweak thereof.Pleasantly, one can arrive at the correct statement using only what we have discussed so far about local geometric Langlands.Let us see how.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: To begin, recall that for any ˇG oper χ, with underlying local system σ, local geometric Langlands predicts that the categorical loop group representation Cσ corresponding to Vect ≃QCoh(pt) under the map σ : pt →LocSys ˇ G may be obtained by renormalizing bgκ -mod ⊗ QCoh(Op ˇ G) Vect, i.e., Kac–Moody representations with central character χ.Remark 6.9.4.Now that we have discussed ind-coherent sheaves of categories, this renormalization may be understood as a consequence of the formal smoothness of the map Op ˇ G →LocSys ˇ G, which, in particular, implies that the sub-2-category generated by QCoh(Op ˇ G) consists solely of quasi- coherent sheaves of categories.That is, there is no room for nontrivial singular support.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the Langlands dual side, this predicts that bgκc -mod is tempered, i.e., that the canonical map D-mod(LG/LN, ψ) ⊗ D-mod(LN,ψ\LG/LN,ψ) Wκc -mod →bgκc -mod is an equivalence.This is a remarkable conjecture about Kac–Moody representations at critical level.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.9.5.Let us specialize the previous discussion, which applies to any local system σ, to the trivial connection.For this, we may tautologically factor σ as pt →pt / ˇG →LocSys ˇ G .We have already discussed in some detail what QCoh(pt / ˇG) is meant to correspond to under local geometric Langlands, namely D-modules on the aﬃne Grassmannian.This gives an alternative presentation of Cσ, as follows.Since pt / ˇG →LocSys ˇ G is as far from smooth as possible, we have that Vect lies in the category generated by QCoh(pt / ˇG).That is, we ﬁnd that Vect ≃QCoh(pt / ˇG) Hom2-IndCohnilp(LocSys ˇ G)(QCoh(pt / ˇ G),QCoh(pt / ˇ G)) Hom2-IndCohnilp(LocSys ˇ G)(QCoh(pt / ˇG), QCoh(pt)) ≃QCoh(pt / ˇG) IndCohnilp(pt / ˇ pt / ˇ G) IndCohnilp(pt pt).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Therefore, on the automorphic side, we should have that Cσ ≃D-mod(GrG) IndCohnilp(pt / ˇ pt / ˇ G) IndCohnilp(pt pt).(6.29) As tensoring from IndCohnilp(pt / ˇG pt / ˇG) to IndCohnilp(pt pt) is simply forgetting equivari- ance for the action of ˇG, we may rewrite this more plainly as Cσ ≃D-mod(GrG) QCoh(pt / ˇ G) QCoh(pt).(6.30) Explicitly, this is the category of Hecke eigensheaves on the aﬃne Grassmannian.That is, recall that QCoh(pt / ˇG), i.e., Rep( ˇG), is identiﬁed with the abelian Satake category D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G)♥.This category acts via right convolution on D-modules on the aﬃne Grassmannian, which we denote by − L+G ⋆ −: D-mod(LG/L+G) ⊗D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G) →D-mod(LG/L+G).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Our desired category consists of eigenobjects for this action, i.e., sheaves F on D-mod(GrG) equipped with compatible isomorphisms (6.31) F L+G ⋆ Sat(V ) ≃F ⊗Oblv(V ), for V ∈Rep( ˇG), where Oblv(V ) denotes the underlying vector space of V .A basic observation to make about such an F, for which convolution with any Satake sheaves returns a direct sum of copies of F, is that F must have inﬁnite dimensional support and, in particular, cannot be a compact object of D-mod(GrG).Before comparing the two descriptions of Cσ, let us make a couple more orienting comments.Remark 6.9.6.One arrives at the more down to earth formulation (6.31) of Hecke eigensheaves by dragging the Satake sheaf through the tensor product (6.30), i.e., by considering (F L+G ⋆ V ) ⊗k ≃F ⊗(V · k) ≃F ⊗Oblv(V ), where · denotes the action of QCoh(pt / ˇG) on QCoh(pt).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Remark 6.9.7.The reader meeting these ideas for the ﬁrst time may ﬁnd some of the details of the preceding discussion somewhat involved.It is therefore worth emphasizing that one can also predict this by analogy.Namely, in the p-adic case, to extract an irreducible unramiﬁed representation πη of G(Fq((t))) from Fun(G(Fq((t)))/G(Fq[[t]])),

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS one passes to eigenvectors for the right action of the spherical Hecke algebra with eigenvalue η, i.e., the corresponding homomorphism η : Fun(G(Fq[[t]])\G(Fq((t)))/G(Fq[[t]]))) →k.In the geometric setting, there is only one possible eigenvalue by Tannaka duality, namely the monoidal functor Oblv : Rep( ˇG) →Vect, and we are again building the irreducible unramiﬁed representation from the universal one by passing to eigenvectors.In particular, the observation we made about the support of Hecke eigensheaves above lifts an analogous assertion about the support of Hecke eigenvectors. 6.9.8.By comparing the two constructions of Cσ in the unramiﬁed case, one obtains the following prediction.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Namely, for any oper structure χ on the trivial connection, there should be an equivalence (6.32) D-mod(GrG) ⊗ QCoh(pt / ˇ G) QCoh(pt) ≃bgκc -modχ, where the right hand side denotes an appropriate renormalization of the category of Kac–Moody represen- tations with central character χ.This is in fact an important theorem,31 whose development involved signiﬁcant contributions from multiple groups of authors over several decades.A brief history is as follows.In their work on quantization of the Hitchin system [BD], Beilinson–Drinfeld showed that, under the convolution action D-mod(L+G\LG/L+G) ⊗bgκc -modL+G →bgκc -modL+G, any central quotient of the vacuum module is an eigenobject for the action of the abelian Satake category.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This theorem was the major local input into their construction of Hecke eigensheaves in global geometric Langlands corresponding to global opers. 6.9.9.The implications of Beilinson–Drinfeld’s work for localization theory at critical level were realized by Frenkel–Gaitsgory, and substantially developed in [FG04], [FG06b], and [FG09c].To begin, the Hecke eigen-property established by Beilinson–Drinfeld was used by Frenkel–Gaitsgory to construct a functor (6.33) D-mod(GrG) ⊗ QCoh(pt / ˇ G) QCoh(pt) →bgκc -modχ .Roughly, this amounted to showing that the global sections of any D-module on GrG (twisted by the critical line bundle, so that one obtains a representation at critical level, and with the central quotient corresponding to χ imposed) is naturally a Hecke eigenobject.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For delta D-modules, this is exactly the previous theorem of Beilinson–Drinfeld, and the general case may be reduced to this one.In addition to conjecturing that (6.33) should be a t-exact equivalence, Frenkel–Gaitsgory established many of its fundamental properties.Namely, they proved that it was right t-exact and a fully faithful embedding on bounded below derived categories.32 They moreover proved that it was an equivalence on I-equivariant objects, i.e., highest weight modules.Remark 6.9.10.With a little work, one obtains from these results the analog of the Kazhdan–Lusztig con- jecture for the characters of simple highest weight modules at critical level.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This was conjectured by Feigin– Frenkel, see [AF12], and is proven in [DY]. 31More carefully, it is a theorem at least under the assumption that χ corresponds to an oper on the formal punctured disk, cf.Example 6.8.24.However, it is expected that the general case may be handled similarly. 32The fully faithfulness in general and, in particular, the correct renormalization of the category of Kac–Moody representa- tions, was later obtained by Raskin [Ras20a].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON 6.9.11.After the work of Frenkel–Gaitsgory, the remaining pieces of their conjecture were that (6.33) was t-exact and essentially surjective.The latter is proﬁtably reinterpreted as a generation statement under the categorical action of the loop group as follows.The left hand side of (6.33) is by deﬁnition generated by its L+G-equivariant objects.Therefore, it remained to show the same held for the right hand side.On the one hand, this is a fairly natural sounding statement.Indeed, the central character imposed is of unramiﬁed nature, corresponding to an oper on the formal non-punctured disk, and so it is rather plausible that the category itself should be unramiﬁed.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: However, this proved to be a diﬃcult assertion, in large part due to how little was, and largely still is, explicitly known about Kac–Moody representations beyond tame ramiﬁcation. 6.9.12.Over a decade later, signiﬁcant progress was made by Raskin [Ras20a], who proved the conjecture in the ﬁrst nontrivial case of GL2 and, in fact, for any group of semisimple rank one.To do so, he proved a general assertion about categorical representations of LGL2, namely their generation by Whittaker and Iwahori invariants, which parallels an earlier and similarly fundamental assertion in the p-adic theory.As (6.33) is an equivalence on such objects, the full equivalence then follows.The general case of the conjecture was then settled by Raskin–Yang [RY].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The major new ingredient was the adaptation of Moy–Prasad theory from the p-adic setting by Yang [Yan21];see also the earlier [CK17].Crucially, besides the ﬁltration of loop group representations by depth, Moy–Prasad theory moreover provided an explicit list of compact generators for each successive quotient, corresponding to unreﬁned minimal K-types in the p-adic theory.Their proof then showed by a nontrivial analysis that having a nonzero map from any such generator beyond depth zero is incompatible with an unramiﬁed central character, which yielded the desired essential surjectivity.Remark 6.9.13.In fact, a crucial technical point, which we have swept under the rug in the preceding discussion, is that the category bgκc -modχ does not carry an a priori categorical action of LG due to its renormalization.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This is one of the basic diﬃculties surmounted in [RY].Remark 6.9.14.We would like to make a remark on Moy–Prasad theory in geometric Langlands, which is otherwise independent of our discussion of localization.Namely, an interesting feature of working with ˇG-connections as opposed to Galois representation, due to Bremer–Sage [BS13], [Sag17], [BS18], is that one also has a theory of minimal K-types for ˇG-connections.The interaction with local geometric Langlands and particularly Moy–Prasad theory on the automorphic side is not yet fully understood. 6.9.15.Let us ﬁnish our discussion of localization theory at critical level with two comments.First, as the reader may imagine, the above admits an extension from the unramiﬁed case to the case of tame ramiﬁcation, e.g., with unipotent monodromy.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This was developed by Frenkel and Gaitsgory in [FG06b] and [FG09a], roughly by passing from the aﬃne Grassmannian to the aﬃne ﬂag variety.Second, it is rather arresting that, given the remarkable nature of the localization theorem at critical level we have discussed, it is in some sense the tip of the iceberg.That is, it is expected that many of the known constructions of irreducible representations of p-adic groups of higher depth should admit geometric versions, leading to equivalences and, in particular, localization theorems for critical level representations with wildly ramiﬁed central characters;see [FG06b] and [KS15] for some discussion and conjectures in this direction.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: In particular, the surveyor expects that, for an oper whose underlying local system admits a ˇB-reduction, the corresponding category of Kac–Moody modules localizes as a category of twisted D-modules on the semi-inﬁnite ﬂag manifold.For ramiﬁed characters, such a localization is no longer possible also on the aﬃne ﬂag variety as in [FG09a], but instead on the quotient by a smaller compact open subgroup ﬁrst introduced in the p-adic setting by Roche [Roc98]. 6.10.Siblings.In this section, we have discussed the local geometric Langlands conjecture, and hopefully the reader has gained a basic feeling for its statement and some of its concrete predictions in representation theory and geometry, both known and conjectural.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Before we ﬁnish, we should mention some important variants or, rather, sibling conjectures in nearby areas, as well as some other emerging connections. 6.10.1.Quasi-split groups.The ﬁrst comment we should make is that we have worked throughout this survey with loop groups, i.e., split reductive groups over k((t)).However, even for the study of their categorical representations, as in number theory, it is important to also consider the case of twisted loop groups, i.e., the analogues of quasi-split groups in the p-adic setting.Note this allows for a similar picture of the representation theory of twisted aﬃne Lie algebras, and the forms of local geometric Langlands duality discussed below again are expected to extend to the quasi-split case. 6.10.2.Quantum local geometric Langlands.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Recall that bgκ -mod is a categorical representation of the loop group only for integral levels.For other levels, it instead carries an action of the category of twisted D- modules D-modκ(LG).One can ask if there is a form of local Langlands duality for such twisted categorical representations of loop groups.Indeed there is, and this is the subject of quantum geometric Langlands.To proceed, let us for simplicity assume that κ −κc is a nondegenerate bilinear form.In this case, one may attach a dual form ˇκ for ˇG, as follows.If we write κˇg,c for the critical level for ˇg, then ˇκ is deﬁned by the property that κ −κc and ˇκ −κˇg,c are dual bilinear forms on t and ˇt, respectively.That is, up to the critical shift we have repeatedly met throughout, one asks that κ and ˇκ be dual forms.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The local quantum Langlands conjecture, due to Gaitsgory [Gai07], is that one has an equivalence of (∞, 2)-categories D-modκ(LG) -mod ≃D-mod−ˇκ(L ˇG) -mod .This builds on earlier work in the global setting, due to Beilinson–Drinfeld, Feigin–Frenkel, and Stoyanovsky [Sto06].We conﬁne ourselves here to only a few comments;see however [Gai18b], [ABC+18] for more details.Remark 6.10.3.A basic thing to notice about the quantum case is that the two sides look more symmetric, as they only concern twisted categorical loop group representations.Moreover, in a precise sense, one recovers the usual statement (6.19) in the limit as κ →κc, and hence ˇκ →∞, and one recovers its analogue with the roles of G and ˇG reversed in the limit as ˇκ →κˇg,c, and hence κ →∞.Remark 6.10.4.The adjective ‘quantum’ arises as follows.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Recall the Feigin–Frenkel isomorphism Wg,κc ≃OOp ˇ G, which plays a basic role in the story at critical level.In fact, Feigin–Frenkel showed in [FF91] that this is the quasi-classical limit of a family of isomorphisms of aﬃne W-algebras Wg,κ ≃Wˇg,ˇκ.These isomorphisms, now between non-commutative algebras, deformation quantize the previous isomor- phism and play a basic role in the quantum theory.Relatedly, while at critical level we saw that the representations of the dual group Rep( ˇG) play a basic role in the unramiﬁed cases of geometric Langlands, the analogous role is played in the quantum setting by representations of the quantum group Repq( ˇG). 6.10.5.Connections with physics.So far, we have only touched on some of the relations between geometric Langlands and physics and mostly on ties to two-dimensional conformal ﬁeld theory.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: However, there is an extremely rich connection with three- and four-dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories, starting with the works [KW07], [Wit08], [GW08], [FW08].This is the source of many interesting constructions and expected compatibilities in (quantum) geometric Langlands, both local and global.We refer the reader to [Gai18a], [GR19], [BFN18], [Gai19], [CG19], [CG20], [CGL20], [FG20], [BFGT21], [HR21] for a partial indication of recent work, as well as the forthcoming [GY].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON Remark 6.10.6.One exciting aspect of some of the above work is its close relation to new developments in the arithmetic Langlands program.Namely, many predictions of Langlands dual categories coming from S-duality of boundary conditions for four-dimensional N = 4 Yang–Mills, as studied by Gaiotto– Witten [GW09], match analogous predictions in arithmetic, notably from the relative Langlands program of Sakellaridis–Venkatesh [SV17].This connection is developed in ongoing work of Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis– Venkatesh. 6.10.7.We have arrived at our ﬁnal point, which we state ﬁrst somewhat informally.When working with constructible sheaves on algebraic varieties, there are diﬀerent categories of sheaves one can choose that behave similarly.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Plainly, one typically works with either (i) D-modules, for which the corresponding cohomology theory, i.e., global sections of the ‘constant sheaf,’ is algebraic de Rham cohomology;(ii) ℓ-adic sheaves, for which the corresponding cohomology theory is ´etale cohomology;and (iii) when working over the complex numbers, constructible sheaves in the analytic topology, for which the corresponding cohomology theory is singular, i.e., Betti cohomology.In the version of (quantum) geometric Langlands we have discussed, the constructible parts of the cor- respondence are of de Rham type.That is, on the automorphic side we study D-modules on the moduli of G-bundles, and on the spectral side we study coherent sheaves on the moduli of ˇG-bundles with ﬂat connections, i.e., local systems in the de Rham sense.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Relatedly, for a smooth projective curve X over k, the global conjecture, in its modern formulation by Arinkin–Gaitsgory [AG15a], posits an equivalence D-mod(BunG(X)) ≃IndCohnilp(LocSys ˇ G(X)).As we now describe, there are also versions of the theory of ´etale and Betti ﬂavors. 6.10.8.Local geometric Langlands with restricted variation.An important recent development in local arith- metic Langlands has been its formulation in families of representations, i.e. for whole categories and not only irreducible by irreducible [EH14], [Hel21], [Zhu21], [FS21].That is, its modern formulation is roughly as an equivalence between all representations of G(Fq((t))) and coherent sheaves on an appropriate moduli space of Galois representations.Remark 6.10.9.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: In fact, in the spirit of the work of Zelevinsky, Lusztig, and Vogan [Vog93], the automorphic side is subtler and is instead also glued with the categories of representations of other groups, e.g., certain inner forms of G.In the series of works [AGK+20b], [AGK+20a], [AGK+21], Arinkin–Gaitsgory–Kazhdan–Raskin–Rozenblyum– Varshavsky have produced a global categorical geometric Langlands conjecture that makes sense both in characteric zero and over function ﬁelds.It takes the form (6.34) Shv´etale nilp (BunG(X)) ≃IndCohnilp(LocSysrestr ˇ G (X)).On the left hand side, one is considering ind-constructible ℓ-adic sheaves on the moduli of G-bundles on a global curve X with singular support in the global nilpotent cone of T ∗BunG(X).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: On the right hand side, one meets ind-coherent sheaves with nilpotent singular support on an appropriately deﬁned moduli space of ℓ-adic ˇG local systems on X.Remark 6.10.10.Very roughly speaking, the basic picture is that, over the complex numbers, the spectral side looks like a ‘torn apart’ version of the Betti moduli stack of ˇG-local systems, i.e., the moduli space parametrizing representations of the topological fundamental group.That is, one decomposes the Betti stack into many pieces based on the semisimpliﬁcation of the local system and takes the disjoint union of their formal neighborhoods.For example, the formal neighborhood of an irreducible local system is isolated in LocSysrestr ˇ G and identiﬁes with the corresponding formal completion in the Betti or de Rham moduli spaces.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Relatedly, the superscript ‘restr’ stands for restricted variation.In the function ﬁeld setting, upon taking the categorical trace of Frobenius, this was shown to recover (compactly supported) automorphic forms and, in particular, the automorphic-to-Galois direction of unram- iﬁed global Langlands for cuspidal representations over function ﬁelds.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS In unpublished work, Gaitsgory has formulated a local version of (6.34).This roughly asserts an equiva- lence Shv´etale(G(Fq((t))) -mod ≃2-IndCohnilp(LocSysrestr ), where on the left hand side one really works with a subtler notion of categorical representation to correct the non-essential surjectivity of the fully faithful embedding Shv´etale(X) ⊗Shv´etale(Y )֒ →Shv´etale(X × Y ) and passes further to a full subcategory of ‘spectrally ﬁnite’ objects.Via a categorical trace of Frobenius, this is expected in the function ﬁeld setting to recover a form of the arithmetic local Langlands conjecture in its formulation by Zhu [Zhu21]. 6.10.11.Local Betti geometric Langlands.Finally, a version of geometric Langlands for Betti sheaves has been formulated by Ben-Zvi–Nadler [BZN18].

text: We hope the reader has gained a feel for some of the basic ideas, results, and conjectures in this area, as well as some appreciation for their beauty.The interested reader is encouraged to wade into the literature we have toured, and, as is particularly feasible in an area with so many attractive open problems, further learn by doing.Appendix A.From functions on X(Fq) to D-modules on X(C) A.1.Overview.A.1.1.The goal of this appendix, which is a supplement to Section 3, is to explain in what sense passing from functions on the Fq-points of the ﬂag variety to D-modules on the C-points of the ﬂag variety is a natural thing to do.The short answer is that one thinks of the latter as some sort of categoriﬁcation of the former.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON We hope the following presentation of these topics gives enough context and intuition for nonspecialists to appreciate the discussion in the main body of the text.We will defer the suggestion of references to the end of each subsection.A.2.Algebraic D-modules.A.2.1.In this subsection we would like to discuss the basics of D-modules.We begin with the aﬃne case.So, suppose X is a smooth and aﬃne algebraic variety over a ﬁeld k, which for simplicity we take to be of characteristic zero.Informally, a D-module on X is something in which it makes sense to scale by functions on X and to diﬀerentiate by vector ﬁelds on X.More formally, let us denote by OX the algebra of regular functions on X, and by TX the OX-module of regular vector ﬁelds on X.A D-module M on X is then an OX-module equipped with a ﬂat connection.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: That is, M is a vector space equipped with an action of the algebra of functions OX ⊗M →M, f ⊗m 7→f · m, as well an action by the Lie algebra of vector ﬁelds TX ⊗M →M, ξ ⊗m 7→ξ · m.That the above is a Lie algebra action is exactly the assumption of ﬂatness, i.e., vanishing curvature.These two operations are asked to be compatible with scaling vector ﬁelds by functions f · (ξ · m) = (f · ξ) · m and with diﬀerentiating functions by vector ﬁelds, i.e., to satisfy the ‘Leibnitz rule’ ξ · (f · m) = (ξ · f) · m + f · (ξ · m), where ξ · f denotes the derivative of f with respect to ξ.Equivalently, one can form the algebra DX of polynomial linear diﬀerential operators on X, i.e., the subalgebra of all endomorphisms of OX generated by multiplication by functions and diﬀerentiation by vector ﬁelds.With this, a D-module is simply a left DX-module.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Example A.2.2.For the aﬃne space X = An k, the regular functions and vector ﬁelds take the form OX ≃k[x1, . . . , xn] and TX ≃⊕ i OX · ∂i, where the ∂i, 1 ⩽i ⩽n, denote the standard coordinate vector ﬁelds associated to the coordinates xi.In this case, DX is generated as a k-algebra by xi, ∂j, 1 ⩽i, j ⩽n, subject to the standard commutation relations [xi, xj] = [∂i, ∂j] = 0, [∂i, xj] = ( if i = j, otherwise.Explicitly, DX has as a basis the ordered monomials xa1 1 · · · xan n · ∂b1 1 · · · ∂bn n , for ai, bj ∈Z⩾0, i.e., consists of linear diﬀerential operators with polynomial coeﬃcients.We write D-mod(X)♥for the abelian category of D-modules on X and denote its unbounded derived category by D-mod(X).Let us discuss three basic objects of either category, i.e., examples of D-modules.Example A.2.3.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The algebra of diﬀerential operators DX is naturally a left module over itself, i.e., a D- module.Next, we turn to a slightly less tautological example of ‘global nature.’

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Example A.2.4.For any X, the ring of regular functions OX carries a tautological structure of a D-module.Namely, one multiplies and diﬀerentiates functions in the standard way.This module admits the following presentation via generators and relations.Acting on the constant function 1 yields an isomorphism of D-modules DX/DX · TX ≃OX.In particular, giving a map of D-modules OX →M is the same as specifying a ﬂat section of M, i.e., an element m annihilated by TX.More generally, any vector bundle E equipped with a ﬂat connection ∇is a D-module, and giving a map of D-modules E →M is the same as specifying a ﬂat section of the tensor product M ⊗ OX E∨ equipped with its natural ﬂat connection.Finally, we would like to describe a class of examples of ‘local nature.’ Example A.2.5.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For any closed point x of X, one has an associated delta function D-module.Namely, if we write mx ⊂OX for the maximal ideal of functions vanishing at x, we set δ′ x := DX/(DX · mx).In particular, giving a map of D-modules δ′ x →M is the same as specifying a section of M annihilated by mx, i.e., scheme-theoretically supported at x.The D-module δ′ x is an algebro-geometric version of the vector space of distributions supported at x.34 Relatedly, if ξ1, . . . , ξn are a collection of vector ﬁelds in TX whose image in the tangent space TxX at x forms a basis, then the images of the monomials (A.1) ξa1 1 · · · ξan n , for ai ∈Z⩾0 form a basis for δ′ x.One thinks of the image of 1 from DX as the usual delta distribution, and the entire module is then spanned by its derivatives.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Here is a somewhat technical point, which the reader may safely ignore at ﬁrst pass.It turns out to be better to twist the underlying vector space of δ′ x by a line, namely the determinant of the tangent space at x: δx := δ′ x ⊗ k det(TxX).The reason is as follows.Given a map f : X →Y of smooth aﬃne varieties, one has an associated pushforward of D-modules f∗: D-mod(X) →D-mod(Y ), cf.Section A.2.7 below.When we incorporate the twist, we then have canonical isomorphisms f∗(δx) ≃δf(x), for x ∈X.That is, delta functions pushforward to delta functions, as one expects from the distributional analogue.Remark A.2.6.Here is an alternative construction of δx, which may help elucidate the appearance of the determinant line.Consider the Lie algebra of vector ﬁelds vanishing at x, i.e., mx · TX ⊂TX.This acts naturally on the quotient TX/mx · TX ≃TxX.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Explicitly, the action factors through mx · TX/m2 x · TX ≃T ∗ xX ⊗TxX ≃End(T ∗ xX), and the action on TxX is simply the natural action, for any vector space W, of its Lie algebra of endomor- phisms End(W) on the dual vector space W ∗. 34This parallel is improved by passing to the corresponding right D-module, but the reader may wish to ignore this point.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON Consider the induced action of mx · TX on the determinant line det(TxX).This line also carries a natural action of OX, and these two actions deﬁne an action of the subalgebra DX,x of DX generated by OX and mx · TX.A point here is that, before passing to the determinant, the relevant compatibilities would not be satisﬁed.Finally, the induced D-module is equipped with a canonical isomorphism DX ⊗ DX,x det(TxX) ≃δx, which acts as the identity on the generating determinant lines, i.e., we have described the action of DX,x on the span of the delta distribution itself.As the reader may guess, many D-modules have behavior which interpolates between the last two examples.That is, they resemble an algebraic connection along a subvariety and a delta D-module along its normal directions.A.2.7.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Given a map X →Y of smooth aﬃne varieties, one has natural pullback and pushforward functors between their categories of D-modules, i.e., f !: D-mod(Y ) →D-mod(X) and f∗: D-mod(X) →D-mod(Y ).As for the nature of the functors, for our purposes it suﬃces to bear the following in mind.On a manifold M, one has the algebra of smooth functions and its dual space of distributions.Given a map M →N, one can pull back functions and dually push forward distributions.Intuitively, f !records, for a function on Y satisfying a linear PDE, the linear PDEs satisﬁed by its pullback.Similarly, f∗records, for a distribution on X satisfying a linear PDE, the linear PDEs satisﬁed by its pushforward.In particular, f !and f∗are not always adjoint functors, but rather are dual.This can be made precise using duality of dg-categories as in Section 4.4.3.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: We now provide a more detailed discussion of f !and f∗for the reader’s convenience, though they may safely skip this.The pullback f !is simply given by the quasi-coherent pullback up to a cohomological shift, i.e., f !(M) ≃OX ⊗ OY M[dX −dY ], where we denote by dX and dY the dimensions of X and Y , respectively.Here, OX acts in the tautological way, and TX acts via the chain rule, i.e., via the map TX →OX ⊗ OY TY and the natural action of the latter on f !(M).To describe f∗, note the previous formula for the pullback can be rewritten as tensoring over DY with the bimodule OX ⊗ OY DY .The same bimodule also deﬁnes the pushforward functor f∗.More carefully, it yields a functor between categories of right D-modules fr,∗: mod-D(X) →mod-D(Y ).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The discrepancy is bridged by the fact that left D-modules and right D-modules are canonically identiﬁed.Namely, on a smooth aﬃne variety Z, the canonical bundle KZ carries a natural right action of DZ.Roughly, one thinks of the canonical bundle as an algebraic substitute for distributions and the action is by integration by parts.Tensoring by it deﬁnes the desired equivalence −⊗ OZ KZ : D-mod(Z) ≃mod-D(Z), and applying this on both sides we obtain the pushforward f∗: D-mod(X) ≃mod-D(X) →mod-D(Y ) ≃D-mod(Y ).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS A.2.8.The previous deﬁnition of a D-module in the aﬃne case globalizes straightforwardly, as follows.Suppose now X is a smooth algebraic variety over k, not necessarily aﬃne.A D-module M on X is a quasi-coherent sheaf M equipped with a ﬂat connection.That is, if we write OX for the sheaf of regular functions, TX for the sheaf of regular ﬁelds, and k for the constant sheaf associated to k, M is a sheaf of k vector spaces equipped with maps OX ⊗ k M →M and TX ⊗ k M →M, satisfying compatibilities as in the previous section.We recall that quasicoherence is the further condition that, for any aﬃne open U and regular function f on U with nonvanishing locus Uf, the natural map Γ(U, M) ⊗ OU OUf ∼ −→Γ(Uf, M) is an isomorphism.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: By this assumption, if X is aﬃne, the present sheaf-theoretic category of D-modules is canonically equivalent to the one of the previous subsection, via the functor of taking global sections.So, somewhat informally, the category of D-modules on a general smooth variety is glued from the previ- ously discussed categories of D-modules on its aﬃne open subvarieties.Similarly, a D-module M is roughly a sheaf whose local sections one can scale by regular functions and diﬀerentiate by regular vector ﬁelds.The examples of the previous subsection carry over to this setting as follows.Example A.2.9.One has a global sheaf DX of diﬀerential operators on X, and D-modules are quasicoherent sheaves of DX-modules.Example A.2.10.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For any X, the sheaf of regular functions OX is naturally a D-module, as is the sheaf of sections of any vector bundle with ﬂat connection (E, ∇).Example A.2.11.For an closed point x of X, one again has a delta function D-module supported at x, which we denote by δx.A.2.12.Finally, we note that the D-modules on X, as discussed in Section A.2.8, naturally form an abelian category in such a way that the forgetful functor to sheaves of abelian groups is t-exact.That is, one calculates kernels, cokernels, and direct sums in the usual way for sheaves, and these naturally inherit structures of D-modules and satisfy the correct universal properties.Deﬁnition A.2.13.We write D-mod(X)♥for the abelian category of D-modules on X.We denote its unbounded derived category by D-mod(X).

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Given a map f : X →Y , one again has pushforward and pullback functors f !: D-mod(Y ) →D-mod(X) and f∗: D-mod(X) →D-mod(Y ), deﬁned as in Section A.2.7.We should highlight that in the non-aﬃne case, f∗is the composite of the left derived functor of tensoring with the bimodule OX ⊗ OY DY and the right derived functor of pushforward of sheaves along f.As such, it is not the derived functor of a functor between abelian categories of D-modules, and requires working with derived categories from the outset.A.2.14.For further reading on D-modules, the reader may consult, as some of many possible references, ordered roughly by increasing demands on the reader, [Cou95], [AN12], [Ber82], [Kas03], [Gai05], [HTT08].A.3.The functions-sheaves correspondence.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON A.3.1.We have, as promised, made sense of the category of D-modules on the complex ﬂag variety D-mod(FlG(C)).We would like to next explain the sense in which this is analogous to the vector space of functions Fun(FlG(Fq)).A.3.2.For any Fq-variety X and ﬁeld k of characteristic zero, recall we associated to it Fun(X(Fq), k), the vector space of k-valued functions on the ﬁnite set of rational points X(Fq).A wonderful fact of life is that special functions in Fun(X(Fq), k) are often the shadows of special sheaves on X.Let us say this more precisely.A.3.3.To do so, let us take k = Qℓ, an algebraic closure of the ℓ-adic numbers Qℓ, where ℓis any prime number coprime to q.With this choice of k one has a well-behaved category of ´etale local systems of k vector spaces on X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: This category is equivalent to the category of continuous representations of the ´etale fundamental group of X on k vector spaces.Remark A.3.4.Here is an orienting remark for the reader unfamiliar with these notions.Consider a smooth complex algebraic variety X equipped with a local system L, by which we mean a locally constant sheaf of ﬁnite dimensional k vector spaces, in the sense of the analytic topology.The basic observation to make is that one can hardly ever trivialize L on a Zariski open subset of X.Concretely, the reader may wish to think through the case of X = Gm and L a rank one local system whose monodromy around the origin is a root of unity.However, if the corresponding representation of the fundamental group of X factors through a ﬁnite quotient, one can trivialize L after pulling back to a ﬁnite covering space ˜X of X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Crucially, ˜X is again canonically an algebraic variety – we emphasize that this is a nonobvious fact in general.In the previous example, if the monodromy is an nth root of unity, one can take the cover to be Gm →Gm, z 7→zn.The covering map ˜X →X is a prototypical example of an ´etale, i.e., a ﬂat and unramiﬁed, map of algebraic varieties.The upshot is that if one allows oneself to check local properties of sheaves on not just Zariski open sets, but also ´etale covers, one obtains a robust theory of local systems which makes sense for general schemes, not necessarily over the complex numbers.More generally, if one wants to consider local systems also on locally closed subvarieties of X, these all naturally belong to, and in fact generate, the bounded derived category of constructible ´etale sheaves Sh(X)b.A.3.5.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Let us explain what this category looks like in the simplest case of X being a point, i.e., the spectrum of a ﬁeld κ.If κ is separably closed, its constructible derived category of sheaves of k vector spaces is simply the bounded derived category of k vector spaces, i.e.Sh(Spec κ)b ≃Vectb k .Plainly, this is because Spec κ does not have interesting ´etale covers, and this should match the reader’s intuition for what happens for usual sheaves on a point in topology or complex geometry.We emphasize that k plays the role of the coeﬃcients for the sheaves, and κ provides the geometric object Spec κ on which the sheaves live.In particular, there need be no relation between κ and k.However, for a general ﬁeld κ, Spec κ does have interesting ´etale covers.For example, given a separable extension of ﬁelds κ →κ′, the map Spec κ′ →Spec κ

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS is ´etale, and any ﬁnite ´etale cover is a disjoint union of such maps.For this reason, writing κs for a separable closure of κ and H := Gal(κs/κ) for its Galois group, one has a canonical equivalence between constructible sheaves on Spec κ and the bounded derived category of ﬁnite dimensional continuous representations of H on k vector spaces, i.e.Sh(Spec κ)b ≃Repk(H)b.In particular, the category of ´etale sheaves captures arithmetic information about the ﬁeld κ.An analogue to Spec κ in usual topology would not be a point, but rather the classifying space pt /H of a (proﬁnite) group H.In this analogy, one thinks of the map Spec κs →Spec κ as akin to the map pt →pt /H.A.3.6.Given a map f : X →Y of schemes, one has pushforward and pullback functors35 f∗: Sh(X)b →Sh(Y )b and f !

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: : Sh(Y )b →Sh(X)b.Here f∗is the usual pushforward of sheaves, and f !is the so-called exceptional inverse image.If f is a proper map (recall this roughly means that the ﬁbres of the map are projective varieties), f∗is left adjoint to f !.In particular, given a closed point x of X, with residue ﬁeld κx, one has an adjunction ix,∗: Sh(Spec κx)b ⇄Sh(X)b : i!x.Concretely, ix,∗produces skyscraper sheaves supported at x, and its adjoint i!x sends a sheaf to its (derived) sections supported at x.A.3.7.Let X again be a variety over Fq.We are now ready to describe the promised map FF : Sh(X)b →Fun(X(Fq)), which is known as Grothendieck’s functions-sheaves correspondence.For each rational point x : Spec Fq →X, we therefore need to produce a map Sh(X)b →k, i.e., the values of the associated functions at x.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: We remind the reader that, as in Section A.3.3, k denotes the algebraic closure Qℓof the ℓ-adic numbers.To deﬁne the desired evaluation, we ﬁrst pass to the !-stalk at x, i.e., consider the composition Sh(X)b i!x −→Sh(Spec Fq)b ≃Repk(Gal(Fq/Fq))b.From here, we recall that Gal(Fq/Fq) is simply the proﬁnite completion bZ of the integers, with topological generator the Frobenius automorphism Fr.In particular, by taking the trace of Frobenius, we obtain the desired map Sh(X)b i!x −→Repk(Gal(Fq/Fq))b tr(Fr,−) −−−−−→k.Explicitly, this sends a sheaf S to the number Σ j (−1)j · tr(Fr, Hj(i!xS)).Remark A.3.8.In case this seems remote to the reader, let us pursue the analogy of Section A.3.5.Replacing the completion bZ by the usual integers Z, note that pt /Z is simply the circle S1.That is, one can think of Spec Fq as something like a circle.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: One can then think of an n-dimensional variety X →Fq as akin to a 2n + 1 dimensional real manifold ﬁbred over a circle π : M →S1 and its rational points as a collection of embedded circles in M providing sections of π.The analogue of the trace of Frobenius would send a local system on M to the traces of its monodromies about these circles. 35One further has a !-pushforward and a ∗-pullback, but we will not need these.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON A.3.9.A basic property of the functions-sheaves correspondence is that it intertwines the ∗-pushforward of functions with the ∗-pushforward of sheaves and similarly for !-pullbacks.For pullbacks, this is by deﬁnition, but, for pushforwards, one needs the Lefschetz ﬁxed point formula in ´etale cohomology.In addition, since i!sends distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles,36 we obtain a map of k vector spaces FF : K(Sh(X)b) ⊗ Z k →Fun(X(Fq)), where K(−) denotes the Grothendieck group, so that one may reasonably think of Sh(X)b as a ‘categoriﬁ- cation’ of the space of functions.This is a useful point of view, although we mildly caution that the above arrow is typically not an isomorphism.A.3.10.Let us describe two basic examples of the correspondence.Example A.3.11.Let us denote by k the constant sheaf on X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: If X is smooth and n-dimensional, then FF(k) is the constant function on X(Fq) with value qn.Remark A.3.12.Because we work with !-stalks, the sheaf which ‘lifts’ the constant function 1 on any variety X is not the constant sheaf but the dualizing sheaf ωX.This is by deﬁnition obtained by pulling back along the projection π : X →Spec Fq the trivial representation k of Gal(Fq/Fq), i.e. ωX ≃π!(k).The reader should be aware that many authors work instead with the Verdier dual convention, i.e., with ∗-stalks, when setting up the functions-sheaves correspondence, in which case the constant sheaf, and not the dualizing sheaf, would correspond to the constant function 1.Example A.3.13.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Given a rational point x : Spec Fq →X, consider the skyscraper sheaf ix,∗k, where we view k as a trivial Gal(Fq/Fq)-module, concentrated in cohomological degree zero.Then we have FF(ix,∗k) = δx, i.e., the skyscraper sheaf ‘lifts’ the indicator function of the point.Although these simple examples hopefully convey the basic idea to the reader, we should mention that much more interesting numbers and functions, e.g., Gauss sums, Kloosterman sums, and characters of ﬁnite groups of Lie type, have sheaf-theoretic counterparts.Another rich example, which gave birth to the geometric Langlands theory, is the lift of unramiﬁed Hecke eigenfunctions over function ﬁelds to Hecke eigensheaves on moduli spaces of G-bundles on curves over ﬁnite ﬁelds.A.3.14.For further details the reader may wish to consult [Mil89], [Mil80], [FK88].A.4.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The Riemann–Hilbert correspondence.A.4.1.Having passed from Fun(X(Fq)) to Sh(X)b, we can make sense of the latter for X over any base ﬁeld and not just Fq.Over the complex numbers, it will be convenient to work instead with the closely related category of constructible analytic sheaves Sh(Xan)b.Here Xan denotes the analytiﬁcation of X, i.e., its set of closed points X(C) equipped with their metric topology.Explicitly, Sh(Xan)b is the full subcategory of the derived category of sheaves of k vector spaces generated by sheaves that are locally constant along a stratiﬁcation of X into Zariski locally closed subsets. 36Recall that this simply means a sequence A →B →C of maps in Sh(X)b, which up to isomorphism comes from a short exact sequence of complexes.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: More intrinsically, A is the homotopy kernel of B →C, and, equivalently, C is the homotopy cokernel, i.e., cone, of A →B.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS Remark A.4.2.The category Sh(Xan)b is an enlargement of the analogous category of ´etale sheaves, essen- tially by the Artin comparison theorem.For example, if X = Gm, a rank one local system in the ´etale category must have monodromy in the units of the algebraic integers, i.e., Z × ℓ, whereas in the analytic category the monodromy may be any element of Q × ℓ.A.4.3.Finally, let us obtain the desired connection to D-modules.First, ﬁx an isomorphism Qℓ≃C so that we can identify Sh(Xan)b with its analogue with coeﬃcients in complex vector spaces.Recall that Sh(Xan)b contains objects like local systems supported on subvarieties of X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: These may be converted into a full subcategory of D-modules by an elaboration of the operation of passing between systems of diﬀerential equations and their local solutions, as follows.A.4.4.Consider ﬁrst the subcategory of the constructible derived category consisting of local systems on X.Let us assume that X is smooth.In this case, one has an equivalence of categories (A.2) {ﬁnite rank local systems on Xan} ≃{ﬂat holomorphic connections on Xan}, where the right hand side denotes the category of holomorphic vector bundles E equipped with a holomorphic ﬂat connection ∇, in the sense of complex geometry.Let us review how this equivalence works.To go from right to left in (A.2), one sends a connection (E, ∇) to its sheaf of ﬂat sections E∇.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: The point is that for any x ∈X, any vector in the ﬁbre Ex extends in a small analytic ball to a unique ﬂat section.Here one uses both that the connection is ﬂat and that one is allowing analytic, and not merely polynomial solutions, to essentially reduce to the case of ordinary diﬀerential equations.To go from left to right, one sends a local system L to the holomorphic bundle L ⊗ k OXan, with its connection induced by the tautological one on OXan.A.4.5.To make contact with algebraic D-modules on X, note that applying −⊗ OX OXan, i.e., allowing not only polynomial, but also holomorphic sections, yields a natural analytiﬁcation functor (A.3) {ﬂat algebraic connections on X} →{ﬂat holomorphic connections on Xan}.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: We emphasize that, on the left, one is considering objects of algebro-geometric nature and, on the right, objects of a complex analytic nature.If X is proper then the functor (A.3) is an equivalence.This is a consequence of the so-called GAGA (i.e., g´eom´etrie alg´ebrique et g´eom´etrie analytique) theorem.However, if X is non-proper, the functor (A.3) is no longer an equivalence.Namely, it is still essentially surjective, but it typically sends many distinct ﬂat algebraic connections to the same holomorphic connection.The reason is simple and already visible for rank one connections – there are typically many more holomorphic functions than polynomial functions (unlike in the case of X proper), and the diﬀerential equations satisﬁed by them lead to identiﬁcations after analytiﬁcation between distinct algebraic connections.Example A.4.6.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Suppose X = A1 with coordinate z, and consider the left algebraic D-modules DX/(DX · ∂z) and DX/(DX · (∂z −1)).Explicitly, the underlying OX-modules both carry canonical identiﬁcations with OX, given by acting on the image of 1 in DX, and carry the connections ∇= ∂z and ∇= ∂z −1.As algebraic D-modules, they are not isomorphic, but their analytiﬁcations are.Indeed, this follows from the fact that ez is a holomorphic, but not polynomial, function and is, up to scalars, the unique solution to ∂zu = u, i.e., a ﬂat section of the second connection.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON What rectiﬁes the many-to-oneness of (A.3) is the following nontrivial observation.For a given ﬂat holomorphic bundle Ean, among the various algebraic connections E mapping to it, there will be a unique one whose ﬂat sections do not have ‘essential singularities at inﬁnity.’ More precisely, an algebraic connection (E, ∇) on X is said to be regular if, for a smooth compactiﬁcation j : X →X of X, with boundary X \ X a simple normal crossings divisor, the connection form j∗∇on j∗E roughly has at most simple poles on the boundary divisor, cf. [HTT08] for a more careful formulation.It turns out this is independent of the choice of X.Example A.4.7.In the previous example, we may take the compactiﬁcation j : A1 →P1, i.e., we add the point at inﬁnity.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: With respect to the coordinate w = z−1 near inﬁnity, the two connections take the form ∇= ∂w and ∇= ∂w + w−2, respectively.In particular, the second connection has a double pole and so is not regular.This is equivalent to the fact that the function ez has an essential singularity at ∞.When one restricts to regular connections, the analytiﬁcation functor {regular algebraic connections on X} →{ﬂat holomorphic connections on Xan} is an equivalence.The resulting composite equivalence with local systems (A.4) ∇: {regular algebraic connections on X} ≃{ﬁnite rank local systems on Xan} is explicitly given by taking the ﬂat analytic sections.This is known as the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for connections.A.4.8.Finally, let us describe the desired extension of (A.4) to all constructible sheaves on X.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Intuitively, we would like to interchange now not only local systems and regular connections, but also those supported on subvarieties.A ﬁrst guess would be that one has an equivalence of abelian categories between constructible sheaves and a suitable category of D-modules.After all, the previous correspondence for connections matched the abelian categories.For example, one might expect to exchange the constant sheaf CX and the regular functions OX, and, for any closed point x of X, the rank one skyscraper sheaf Cx and the delta D-module δx.However, this cannot literally hold.Indeed, if X is of dimension d > 0, and one looks at the homomorphisms in the abelian category, one has HomSh(Xan)♥(CX, Cx) ≃C but HomD-mod(X)♥(OX, δx) ≃0.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: To correct for this, observe that when passing to derived categories, we have HomSh(Xan)(CX, Cx) ≃C and HomD-mod(X)(OX, δx) ≃C[−d].The reader is encouraged to check both assertions, e.g., for the aﬃne line X = A1.In any case, we see the desired extension will need to involve cohomological shifts and, in particular, must be formulated in terms of derived categories.A.4.9.With this in mind, we are led to the following.The category of regular holonomic D-modules, denoted by D-modrh(X), is the full triangulated subcategory of D-mod(X) generated by ∗-extensions of regular algebraic connections from smooth subvarieties Z ⊂X.One has a functor of (derived) ﬂat analytic sections, deﬁned on the category of all D-modules (A.5) ∇: D-mod(X) →{sheaves of C-vector spaces},

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: CATEGORICAL REPRESENTATIONS AND LOCAL GEOMETRIC LANGLANDS which we shall describe in more detail momentarily.However, the main result here is that (A.5), when restricted to regular holonomic D-modules, factors through the constructible derived category and yields an equivalence (A.6) ∇: D-modrh(X) ≃Sh(Xan)b.This is known as the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for D-modules.A.4.10.Invariantly, (A.5) is deﬁned as follows.The holomorphic canonical bundle ωXan is naturally a right D-module, and (A.5) is obtained by tensoring with it: ∇:= ωXan ⊗ DX −.As with Lie algebra homology, a canonical projective resolution of ωXan yields the following presentation.Let us denote by Ωi an, for 1 ⩽i ⩽d, the sheaves of holomorphic i-forms on X.In particular, note that Ωd an = ωXan.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: With this, (A.5) sends a D-module M, concentrated in cohomological degree zero, to the de Rham complex of sheaves (A.7) M →M ⊗ OX Ω1 an →· · · →M ⊗ OX Ωd an where M is placed in cohomological degree −d.Explicitly, for a local section m of M, and local coordinates z1, . . . , zd on X, the ﬁrst diﬀerential sends m 7→Σ i (∂i · m) ⊗dzi, and similarly for higher diﬀerentials.A complex of D-modules is then sent to the totalization of a corre- sponding de Rham bicomplex.This construction visibly respects quasi-isomorphisms and yields the desired functor (A.5).A.4.11.Let us conclude this discussion with some basic examples and properties.Example A.4.12.The Riemann–Hilbert correspondence sends the structure sheaf to a shift of the constant sheaf, namely ∇(OX) ≃CX[dX].

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: It sends a delta D-module δx to the corresponding skyscraper sheaf, i.e., ∇(δx) ≃Cx.The reader may wish to check these directly and note in particular their compatibility with the discussion of Section A.4.8.More generally, for a smooth subvariety i : Z →X of dimension dZ and a regular connection E on Z with ﬂat analytic sections L, we have ∇(i∗E) ≃i∗L[dZ].A.4.13.It is also possible to treat D-modules on a singular variety X.For any embedding X֒ →S into a smooth variety, this category canonically agrees with the full subcategory of D-modules on S set-theoretically supported on X.The Riemann–Hilbert correspondence again holds for singular varieties and may be deduced from the smooth case.The formulas of Example A.4.12 are then a special case of the following.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: For any map of algebraic varieties X →Y , the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence exchanges ∗-pushforwards and !-pullbacks of D-modules and constructible sheaves.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-21_范畴表示论与局部几何朗兰兹导论/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: GURBIR DHILLON A.4.14.Finally, let us discuss abelian categories.The subcategory D-modrh(X) is closed under the standard truncation functors on D-mod(X) and canonically identiﬁes with the derived category of the corresponding abelian category of regular holonomic D-modules.From Example A.4.12, we see that this abelian category is not exchanged with the standard abelian category of constructible sheaves.Instead, it is identiﬁed with the abelian category of perverse sheaves.A.4.15.For further details, the reader may wish to look at [AN12], [Ber82], [HTT08].Conﬂict of interest.There is no conﬂict of interest.References [AB00] Luchezar Avramov and Ragnar-Olaf Buchweitz, Support varieties and cohomology over complete intersections, Invent.Math. 142 (2000), no. 2, 285–318.

text: arXiv:1602.01451v1 [math.RT] 3 Feb 2016 IAS/Park City Mathematics Series Volume 00, Pages 000–000 S 1079-5634(XX)0000-0 Lectures on Springer theories and orbital integrals Zhiwei Yun Abstract.These are the expanded lecture notes from the author’s mini-course during the graduate summer school of the Park City Math Institute in 2015.The main topics covered are: geometry of Springer ﬁbers, afﬁne Springer ﬁbers and Hitchin ﬁbers;representations of (afﬁne) Weyl groups arising from these objects;relation between afﬁne Springer ﬁbers and orbital integrals.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-22_Springer理论与轨道积分讲义/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Contents Introduction 0.1 Topics of these notes 0.2 What we assume from the readers Lecture I: Springer ﬁbers 1.1 The setup 1.2 Springer ﬁbers 1.3 Examples of Springer ﬁbers 1.4 Geometric Properties of Springer ﬁbers 1.5 The Springer correspondence 1.6 Comments and generalizations 1.7 Exercises Lecture II: Afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 2.1 Loop group, parahoric subgroups and the afﬁne ﬂag variety 2.2 Afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 2.3 Symmetry on afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 2.4 Further examples of afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 2.5 Geometric Properties of afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 2.6 Afﬁne Springer representations 2.7 Comments and generalizations 2.8 Exercises Lecture III: Orbital integrals 3.1 Integration on a p-adic group 3.2 Orbital integrals 3.3 Relation with afﬁne Springer ﬁbers Research supported by the NSF grant DMS-1302071, the Packard Foundation and the PCMI.. ©0000 (copyright holder)

file: 08_source_code/SY02-22_Springer理论与轨道积分讲义/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Lectures on Springer theories and orbital integrals 3.4 Stable orbital integrals 3.5 Examples in SL2 3.6 Remarks on the Fundamental Lemma 3.7 Exercises Lecture IV: Hitchin ﬁbration 4.1 The Hitchin moduli stack 4.2 Hitchin ﬁbration 4.3 Hitchin ﬁbers 4.4 Relation with afﬁne Springer ﬁbers 4.5 A global version of the Springer action 4.6 Exercises 0.Introduction 0.1.Topics of these notes These are the lectures notes from a mini-course that I gave at the PCMI graduate summer school in 2015.The goal is twofold.First I would like to introduce to the audience some interesting geometric objects that have representation-theoretic applications, and Springer ﬁbers and their general- izations are nice examples of such.

file: 08_source_code/SY02-22_Springer理论与轨道积分讲义/工程文件/work/原文/full.txt
text: Second is to introduce orbital integrals with emphasis on its relationship with afﬁne Springer ﬁbers, and thereby supplying background material for B-C.Ngô’s mini-course on the Fundamental Lemmas.The geometric part of these lectures (everything except §3) consists of the study of three types of “ﬁbers”: Springer ﬁbers, afﬁne Springer ﬁbers and Hitchin ﬁbers, with increasing complexity.We will study their geometric properties such as connectivity and irreducible components.We will construct certain group ac- tions on these varieties, and use the action to study several nontrivial examples.Most importantly we will study certain Weyl group actions on the cohomology of these ﬁbers which do not come from actions on the varieties themselves.

text: Zhiwei Yun In these lecture notes we do not try to give complete proofs to all statements but instead to point out interesting phenomena and examples.We do, however, give more or less complete proofs of several key results, such as • Theorem 1.5.1 (the Springer correspondence);• Theorem 2.5.2 (ﬁniteness properties of afﬁne Springer ﬁbers);• Theorem 3.4.8 (cohomological interpretation of stable orbital integrals). 0.2.What we assume from the readers The target readers for these lectures are beginning graduate students interested in geometric representation theory.We assume some basic algebraic geometry (scheme theory, moduli problems, point counting over a ﬁnite ﬁeld, etc) though occasionally we will use the language of algebraic stacks.

text: We also assume some Lie theory (reductive groups over an algebraic closed ﬁeld and over a local ﬁeld), but knowing GLn and SLn should be enough to understand most of these notes.The next remark is about the cohomology theory we use in these notes.Since we work with algebraic varieties over a general ﬁeld k instead of C, we will be us- ing the étale cohomology with coefﬁcients in ℓ-adic sheaves (usually the constant sheaf Qℓ) on these varieties.We denote the étale cohomology of a scheme X over k with Qℓ-coefﬁcients simply by H∗(X).Readers not familiar with étale cohomol- ogy are encouraged to specialize to the case k = C and understand H∗(X) as the singular cohomology of X(C) with Q-coefﬁcients.Perverse sheaves will be used only in §1.5.

text: Acknowledgement I would like to thank the co-organizers, lecturers and the staff of the PCMI summer program in 2015.I would also like to thank the au- dience of my lectures for their feedback.I am especially grateful to Jingren Chi who carefully read through the ﬁrst draft of these notes and provided helpful suggestions. 1.Lecture I: Springer ﬁbers Springer ﬁbers are classical and fundamental objects in geometric representa- tion theory.Springer [46] ﬁrst discovered that their cohomology groups realized representations of Weyl groups, a phenomenon known as the Springer correspon- dence.As singular algebraic varieties, Springer ﬁbers are interesting geometric objects by themselves.They are also connected to the representation theory of ﬁnite groups of Lie type via character sheaves. 1.1.

text: The setup In this section, let k be an algebraically closed ﬁeld.Let G be a connected reductive group over k whose adjoint group is simple (so the adjoint group Gad is determined by one of the seven series of Dynkin diagrams).Assume that char(k) is large compared to G.Let r be the rank of G.

text: Lectures on Springer theories and orbital integrals Sometimes it will be convenient to ﬁx a Cartan subalgebra t of g, or equiva- lently a maximal torus T ⊂G.Once we have done this, we may talk about the roots of the T-action on g.Let B be the ﬂag variety of G: this is the G-homogeneous projective variety parametrizing Borel subgroups of G.Choosing a Borel subgroup B ⊂G, we may identify B with G/B.Let g be the Lie algebra of G.For X ∈g, let CG(X) denote the centralizer of X in G, i.e., the stabilizer at X of the adjoint action of G on g.Let N ⊂g be the subvariety of nilpotent elements.This is a cone: it is stable under the action of Gm on g by scaling.It is known that there are ﬁnitely many G-orbits on N under the adjoint action. 1.2.Springer ﬁbers 1.2.1.
